# Referencia completa de ferramentas — MCPVMWare

Este documento lista **as 1030 ferramentas MCP** do servidor MCPVMWare, cada uma com **descricao** e **sintaxe** (parametros de entrada). E gerado a partir do proprio catalogo do servidor (`tools/list`).

> Gerado por `src/cmd/dumptools` + `scripts/gen_tools_md.py`. Nao editar a mao — regenerar apos mudar tools.

Legenda de modo: `vcenter-only` (so com `--vcenter-url`/`--vmware-all-url`) · `vsphere-general` (tambem em ESXi standalone) · `cloud-aws` · `workstation`. Ferramentas *(destrutiva)* exigem `--allow-destructive` + `confirm:true`.

## vSphere / vCenter / ESXi (907)

### Sistema (1)

#### `vmware_about`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Get information about the connected vCenter/ESXi endpoint (product, version, build, API type, instance UUID).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_about()`

_Sem parametros._

### Alarmes (10)

#### `vmware_alarm_acknowledge`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Acknowledge a triggered alarm on an entity, suppressing further repeat actions for it until the alarm re-triggers from a different state. Reversible only by the alarm re-triggering — vSphere has no un-acknowledge operation.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_alarm_acknowledge(alarm, confirm, [entity, host, vm])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `alarm` | string | sim | The alarm's MoRef value (Type is always "Alarm"), as returned by vmware_alarm_create's "alarm" field or vmware_alarm_get's "alarm" field per entry. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `entity` | object | — | Explicit MoRef of the target ManagedEntity, e.g. {"type": "ClusterComputeResource", "value": "domain-c7"} — use this to target an entity kind vmware_list_vms/vmware_list_hosts can't resolve directly (cluster, datacenter, resource pool, datastore, network, folder, vApp...). Alternative to "vm"/"host". |
| `host` | string | — | Host identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Alternative to "entity"/"vm". |
| `vm` | string | — | VM identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_vms. Alternative to "entity"/"host". |

#### `vmware_alarm_actions_enabled`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Check whether alarm actions are enabled for an entity (and, by inheritance, its descendants).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_alarm_actions_enabled([entity, host, vm])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `entity` | object | — | Explicit MoRef of the target ManagedEntity, e.g. {"type": "ClusterComputeResource", "value": "domain-c7"} — use this to target an entity kind vmware_list_vms/vmware_list_hosts can't resolve directly (cluster, datacenter, resource pool, datastore, network, folder, vApp...). Alternative to "vm"/"host". |
| `host` | string | — | Host identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Alternative to "entity"/"vm". |
| `vm` | string | — | VM identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_vms. Alternative to "entity"/"host". |

#### `vmware_alarm_clear_triggered`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Clear triggered alarm state matching a filter (by severity/entity-type/trigger-type) across the whole inventory. Reversible only by the alarm re-triggering.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_alarm_clear_triggered(confirm, [filter])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `filter` | object | — | AlarmFilterSpec. All fields optional — an empty/omitted filter clears every triggered alarm. "status": array of "gray"\|"green"\|"yellow"\|"red" (filters by triggered severity). "typeEntity": "entityTypeAll"\|"entityTypeHost"\|"entityTypeVm". "typeTrigger": "triggerTypeAll"\|"triggerTypeEvent"\|"triggerTypeMetric". |

#### `vmware_alarm_create`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new alarm definition on a managed entity (VM, host, cluster, datacenter, or any other ManagedEntity). Reversible via vmware_alarm_remove.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_alarm_create(confirm, spec, [entity, host, vm])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `entity` | object | — | Explicit MoRef of the target ManagedEntity, e.g. {"type": "ClusterComputeResource", "value": "domain-c7"} — use this to target an entity kind vmware_list_vms/vmware_list_hosts can't resolve directly (cluster, datacenter, resource pool, datastore, network, folder, vApp...). Alternative to "vm"/"host". |
| `host` | string | — | Host identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Alternative to "entity"/"vm". |
| `spec` | object | sim | AlarmSpec (referencia/govmomi/vim25/types/types.go's AlarmSpec). Required: "name" (string), "enabled" (bool), "expression" (object, see below). Optional: "description" (string), "systemName" (string, predefined alarms only), "actionFrequency" (int32 seconds between repeat actions), "setting" ({"toleranceRange": int32, "reportingFrequency": int32}), "action" (object, see below).  "expression" and "action" are vSphere's polymorphic (xsi:type) fields — encode the concrete type as a JSON object carrying a "_vimType" discriminator naming the exact govmomi struct:   expression._vimType one of:     "EventAlarmExpression"  {"eventTypeId": "...", "objectType": "...", "status": "gray\|green\|yellow\|red", "comparisons": [{"attributeName":"...","operator":"...","value":"..."}]}     "MetricAlarmExpression" {"operator": "isAbove\|isBelow", "type": "<ManagedEntity type>", "metric": {"counterId": int32, "instance": "..."}, "yellow": int32, "yellowInterval": int32, "red": int32, "redInterval": int32}     "StateAlarmExpression"  {"operator": "isEqual\|isUnequal", "type": "<ManagedEntity type>", "statePath": "runtime.powerState", "yellow": "...", "red": "..."}     "AndAlarmExpression" / "OrAlarmExpression"  {"expression": [<nested expression objects, same _vimType convention, recursive>]}   action._vimType one of:     "AlarmTriggeringAction" {"action": <nested BaseAction — see leaf types below>, "transitionSpecs": [{"startState":"green\|yellow\|red","finalState":"green\|yellow\|red","repeats":bool}], "green2yellow": bool, "yellow2red": bool, "red2yellow": bool, "yellow2green": bool}     "GroupAlarmAction"      {"action": [<nested AlarmTriggeringAction objects>]}   action.action (leaf BaseAction) _vimType one of:     "SendEmailAction" {"toList":"a@b.com","ccList":"","subject":"...","body":"..."} \| "SendSNMPAction" {} \| "RunScriptAction" {"script":"/path/to/script"} \| "CreateTaskAction" {"taskTypeId":"...","cancelable":bool} \| "MethodAction" {"name":"...","argument":[{"value":...}]}  See referencia/govmomi/vim25/types/types.go for the exact field set of every nested object (EventAlarmExpressionComparison, PerfMetricId, AlarmTriggeringActionTransitionSpec, MethodActionArgument, ...). |
| `vm` | string | — | VM identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_vms. Alternative to "entity"/"host". |

Alternative to "vm"/"host". |
| `host` | string | — | Host identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Alternative to "entity"/"vm". |
| `vm` | string | — | VM identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_vms. Alternative to "entity"/"host". |

#### `vmware_alarm_reconfigure`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Replace an existing alarm's specification (name/expression/action/etc). Reversible by reconfiguring again with the previous spec.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_alarm_reconfigure(alarm, confirm, spec)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `alarm` | string | sim | The alarm's MoRef value (Type is always "Alarm"), as returned by vmware_alarm_create's "alarm" field or vmware_alarm_get's "alarm" field per entry. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `spec` | object | sim | AlarmSpec (referencia/govmomi/vim25/types/types.go's AlarmSpec). Required: "name" (string), "enabled" (bool), "expression" (object, see below). Optional: "description" (string), "systemName" (string, predefined alarms only), "actionFrequency" (int32 seconds between repeat actions), "setting" ({"toleranceRange": int32, "reportingFrequency": int32}), "action" (object, see below).  "expression" and "action" are vSphere's polymorphic (xsi:type) fields — encode the concrete type as a JSON object carrying a "_vimType" discriminator naming the exact govmomi struct:   expression._vimType one of:     "EventAlarmExpression"  {"eventTypeId": "...", "objectType": "...", "status": "gray\|green\|yellow\|red", "comparisons": [{"attributeName":"...","operator":"...","value":"..."}]}     "MetricAlarmExpression" {"operator": "isAbove\|isBelow", "type": "<ManagedEntity type>", "metric": {"counterId": int32, "instance": "..."}, "yellow": int32, "yellowInterval": int32, "red": int32, "redInterval": int32}     "StateAlarmExpression"  {"operator": "isEqual\|isUnequal", "type": "<ManagedEntity type>", "statePath": "runtime.powerState", "yellow": "...", "red": "..."}     "AndAlarmExpression" / "OrAlarmExpression"  {"expression": [<nested expression objects, same _vimType convention, recursive>]}   action._vimType one of:     "AlarmTriggeringAction" {"action": <nested BaseAction — see leaf types below>, "transitionSpecs": [{"startState":"green\|yellow\|red","finalState":"green\|yellow\|red","repeats":bool}], "green2yellow": bool, "yellow2red": bool, "red2yellow": bool, "yellow2green": bool}     "GroupAlarmAction"      {"action": [<nested AlarmTriggeringAction objects>]}   action.action (leaf BaseAction) _vimType one of:     "SendEmailAction" {"toList":"a@b.com","ccList":"","subject":"...","body":"..."} \| "SendSNMPAction" {} \| "RunScriptAction" {"script":"/path/to/script"} \| "CreateTaskAction" {"taskTypeId":"...","cancelable":bool} \| "MethodAction" {"name":"...","argument":[{"value":...}]}  See referencia/govmomi/vim25/types/types.go for the exact field set of every nested object (EventAlarmExpressionComparison, PerfMetricId, AlarmTriggeringActionTransitionSpec, MethodActionArgument, ...). |

#### `vmware_alarm_remove`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Permanently delete an alarm definition. Irreversible — the alarm and its configuration are gone; re-creating it requires vmware_alarm_create with the same spec.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_alarm_remove(alarm, confirm)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `alarm` | string | sim | The alarm's MoRef value (Type is always "Alarm"), as returned by vmware_alarm_create's "alarm" field or vmware_alarm_get's "alarm" field per entry. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |

### VAMI - Access (16)

#### `vmware_appliance_access_consolecli_get`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Get whether the console-based controlled CLI (TTY1) is enabled on the vCenter Server Appliance. Requires a vCenter Server Appliance — fails against a standalone ESXi host, which has no VAMI (Virtual Appliance Management Interface).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_appliance_access_consolecli_get()`

_Sem parametros._

#### `vmware_appliance_access_consolecli_set`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Enable or disable the console-based controlled CLI (TTY1) on the vCenter Server Appliance. Requires a vCenter Server Appliance — fails against a standalone ESXi host, which has no VAMI (Virtual Appliance Management Interface).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_appliance_access_consolecli_set(confirm, enabled)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `enabled` | boolean | sim | true to enable, false to disable. |

#### `vmware_appliance_access_legacy_consolecli_get`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Get whether the console-based controlled CLI (TTY1) is enabled on the vCenter Server Appliance (VAMI legacy, GET /appliance/access/consolecli). Requires a vCenter Server Appliance — fails against a standalone ESXi host, which has no VAMI (Virtual Appliance Management Interface). LEGACY REST path (/rest/appliance/access/...) — distinct from this project's vmware_appliance_access_* tools (Fase 8a), which target the newer /api/appliance/access/... path via a typed govmomi wrapper. Both control the same underlying appliance setting; use whichever path your target vCenter Server Appliance version actually serves.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_appliance_access_legacy_consolecli_get()`

_Sem parametros._

#### `vmware_appliance_recovery_backup_job_create`

Start a new file-based backup of this vCenter Server Appliance to a remote location (VAMI, POST /appliance/recovery/backup/job). Disruptive to appliance I/O while running; does not alter the running appliance's configuration/state, only produces a new backup artifact. Requires a vCenter Server Appliance — fails against a standalone ESXi host, which has no VAMI (Virtual Appliance Management Interface).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_appliance_recovery_backup_job_create(backup_password, confirm, location, location_type, [comment, location_password, location_user, parts])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `backup_password` | string | sim | Password used to encrypt/protect the backup piece. |
| `comment` | string | — | Free-text comment recorded with the backup job. Optional. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `location` | string | sim | Backup destination URL/path (e.g. an HTTPS/FTPS/SCP/NFS server location). |
| `location_password` | string | — | Password for the backup location, if it requires authentication. Optional. |
| `location_type` | string | sim | Backup location protocol. Typical VAMI values: HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, FTPS, SCP, NFS (not enforced by this tool — whatever this appliance's LocationType enum accepts is forwarded verbatim). |
| `location_user` | string | — | Username for the backup location, if it requires authentication. Optional. |
| `parts` | array&lt;string&gt; | — | Optional backup parts to include beyond the default (e.g. "seat" for statistics/events/alarms/tasks) — see vmware_appliance_recovery_backup_parts for the parts available on this appliance. |

#### `vmware_appliance_recovery_backup_schedule_update`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Replace the configuration of an existing file-based backup schedule (VAMI, PUT /appliance/recovery/backup/schedules/{id}). **Sintaxe:** `vmware_appliance_recovery_backup_schedule_update(backup_password, confirm, enable, location, recurrence_info, retention_info, schedule_id, [location_password, location_user, parts])`

|---|---|:--:|---|
| `backup_password` | string | sim | Password used to encrypt/protect backups produced by this schedule. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `enable` | boolean | sim | Whether this schedule is active. |
| `location` | string | sim | Backup destination URL/path used by this schedule. |

| `location_user` | string | — | Username for the backup location, if it requires authentication. Optional. |
| `parts` | array&lt;string&gt; | — | Optional backup parts to include beyond the default. See vmware_appliance_recovery_backup_parts for the parts available on this appliance. |
| `recurrence_info` | object | sim | Recurrence configuration, forwarded verbatim as-is. Postman documents the shape {"hour": <0-23>, "minute": <0-59>, "days": ["MONDAY", ...]}. |
| `retention_info` | object | sim | Retention configuration, forwarded verbatim as-is. Postman documents the shape {"max_count": <integer>} (maximum number of backups to keep). |
| `schedule_id` | string | sim | ID of the backup schedule to update — from vmware_appliance_recovery_backup_schedule_list. |

### Autenticacao (1)

#### `vmware_authentication_issue`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Exchange a subject token for a newly issued vCenter authentication token (OAuth2 token-exchange style, RFC 8693 semantics — POST /vcenter/tokenservice/token-exchange). This MINTS a real, usable credential — despite the read-sounding name "Issue", it is not a read-only lookup (see this file's top doc comment for why the codegen classifier's default was overridden). Registered at Tier 2 and gated accordingly.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_authentication_issue(confirm, token)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `token` | object | sim | An authentication.TokenIssueSpec JSON object (matching its Go struct's json tags). Required: "subject_token" (the token being exchanged), "subject_token_type" (a URI identifying the subject token's type, e.g. "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token"), "grant_type" (typically "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange"). Optional: "actor_token", "actor_token_type", "requested_token_type", "resource", "scope", "audience". |

### CIS / Tasks (4)

#### `vmware_cis_tasks_get`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Fetch the current status/progress/result of a vAPI/CIS task, without waiting for it to reach any particular state. A single non-looping read.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_cis_tasks_get(task_id, timeout_seconds)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `task_id` | string | sim | ID of the vAPI/CIS task (e.g. as returned in a "task_id" field by another vapi/* tool in this server, such as vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_apply). NOT a vmware_task_* (object.Task/SOAP) moref — these are two distinct task systems, see this file's top doc comment. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | sim | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever. REQUIRED — no default — this call polls a REST endpoint with no server-side timeout of its own. |

#### `vmware_cis_tasks_wait_for_completion`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Block until a vAPI/CIS task reaches any terminal state (anything other than PENDING/RUNNING — i.e. SUCCEEDED, FAILED, or BLOCKED) and return its final info. Returns an error if the task's final status is FAILED.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_cis_tasks_wait_for_completion(task_id, timeout_seconds)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `task_id` | string | sim | ID of the vAPI/CIS task (e.g. as returned in a "task_id" field by another vapi/* tool in this server, such as vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_apply). NOT a vmware_task_* (object.Task/SOAP) moref — these are two distinct task systems, see this file's top doc comment. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | sim | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever. REQUIRED — no default — this call polls a REST endpoint with no server-side timeout of its own. |

#### `vmware_cis_tasks_wait_for_running_or_error`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Block until a vAPI/CIS task's status becomes RUNNING or FAILED specifically (not SUCCEEDED/BLOCKED/PENDING). Known upstream limitation (not a bug in this tool): a task that transitions straight to SUCCEEDED without ever being observed as RUNNING will block until timeout_seconds expires, since SUCCEEDED satisfies neither condition — prefer vmware_cis_tasks_wait_for_completion unless you specifically need to detect the RUNNING transition.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_cis_tasks_wait_for_running_or_error(task_id, timeout_seconds)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `task_id` | string | sim | ID of the vAPI/CIS task (e.g. as returned in a "task_id" field by another vapi/* tool in this server, such as vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_apply). NOT a vmware_task_* (object.Task/SOAP) moref — these are two distinct task systems, see this file's top doc comment. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | sim | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever. REQUIRED — no default — this call polls a REST endpoint with no server-side timeout of its own. |

#### `vmware_cis_tasks_wait_for_running_or_terminal_state`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Block until a vAPI/CIS task leaves the PENDING state — i.e. its status becomes RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, or BLOCKED. Returns an error if the task's final observed status is FAILED.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_cis_tasks_wait_for_running_or_terminal_state(task_id, timeout_seconds)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `task_id` | string | sim | ID of the vAPI/CIS task (e.g. as returned in a "task_id" field by another vapi/* tool in this server, such as vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_apply). NOT a vmware_task_* (object.Task/SOAP) moref — these are two distinct task systems, see this file's top doc comment. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | sim | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever. REQUIRED — no default — this call polls a REST endpoint with no server-side timeout of its own. |

#### `vmware_cluster_configure_hci`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Run the HCI (hyper-converged infrastructure) quickstart workflow on a cluster: network (DVS/portgroup), host service, and vCenter/EVC configuration in one step. Hosts not already in maintenance mode are skipped unless allowed via cluster_spec/host_inputs; skipped hosts are reported in the result's failedHosts. See this file's top doc comment for cluster_spec.vSanConfigSpec's opaque-passthrough limitation (only dynamicType/dynamicProperty are transported; no concrete vSAN reconfig spec type is vendored here).

| `cluster_spec` | object | sim | A types.ClusterComputeResourceHCIConfigSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields: dvsProf (array), hostConfigProfile, vSanConfigSpec (opaque — see this tool's description), vcProf. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host_inputs` | array&lt;object&gt; | — | Optional array of types.ClusterComputeResourceHostConfigurationInput JSON objects ({"host": {"type":"HostSystem","value":"..."}, "hostVmkNics": [...], "allowedInNonMaintenanceMode": false}). Omit to operate on every host in the cluster. |

Per the underlying API's own result-type doc comment, applying the recommendations is not supported by this call; use the already-existing vmware_host_maintenance_enter (HostSystem.EnterMaintenanceMode_Task) per host to actually do so.

| `hosts` | array&lt;string&gt; | sim | Host identifiers (name/pattern or full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_hosts) to evaluate for maintenance mode. |
| `info` | object | — | Optional types.ClusterComputeResourceMaintenanceInfo JSON object (e.g. {"partialMMId": "..."}) requesting partial maintenance mode instead of full. Requires a sufficiently recent vCenter (8.0.3.0+). |
| `option` | array&lt;object&gt; | — | Optional array of types.OptionValue JSON objects ({"key":..., "value":...}) overriding advanced DRS options for this evaluation. |

|---|---|:--:|---|
| `cluster` | string | sim | Cluster identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cluster-01") or a full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_clusters. Must resolve to exactly one cluster. |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.PlacementSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields — placementType ("create"/"reconfigure"/"relocate"/"clone"), vm {type,value} (for reconfigure/relocate/clone), configSpec, relocateSpec, disk, hosts, datastores, resourcePools, priority. |

#### `vmware_cluster_recommend_hosts_for_vm`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Ask DRS to recommend hosts within a cluster suitable for placing/migrating a virtual machine — a read-only query, distinct from vmware_cluster_place_vm's fuller create/reconfigure/relocate/clone placement spec.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_cluster_recommend_hosts_for_vm(cluster, vm, [pool])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `cluster` | string | sim | Cluster identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cluster-01") or a full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_clusters. Must resolve to exactly one cluster. |
| `pool` | string | — | Optional target ResourcePool name/pattern the VM would be migrated into (see vmware_list_resource_pools). Required by the underlying API when the VM is powered on; this ResourcePool cannot be in the same cluster as the VM. |
| `vm` | string | sim | Virtual machine identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "web-01") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/dc1/vm/web-01") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_cluster_refresh_recommendation`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Force DRS to recompute its host/VM recommendations for a cluster right now, instead of waiting for its next scheduled interval. No configuration change, but classified alongside the cluster's other DRS-recommendation mutating actions here (same convention as vmware_storage_refresh_drs_recommendation for Storage DRS).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_cluster_refresh_recommendation(cluster, confirm)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `cluster` | string | sim | Cluster identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cluster-01") or a full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_clusters. Must resolve to exactly one cluster. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |

#### `vmware_cluster_remove_module_members`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Remove one or more virtual machines from a cluster module. Returns true if every VM was removed, false if any VM was not a member (not an error in that case). Classified tier1 (not tier2, unlike its structural opposite vmware_cluster_add_module_members) per this project's existing tier classification — see this file's top doc comment.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_cluster_remove_module_members(confirm, module_id, vm_paths)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `module_id` | string | sim | Cluster module ID, as returned by vmware_cluster_create_module / vmware_cluster_list_modules. |
| `vm_paths` | array&lt;string&gt; | sim | One or more full inventory paths of VirtualMachine objects (e.g. "/DC0/vm/my-vm"), each resolved via SearchIndex.FindByInventoryPath. Must be non-empty. All VMs must belong to the same vCenter cluster as the module. |

#### `vmware_cluster_retrieve_das_advanced_runtime_info`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Get advanced vSphere HA (DAS) runtime information for a cluster — internal/troubleshooting details beyond what vmware_cluster_configuration's dasConfig exposes.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_cluster_retrieve_das_advanced_runtime_info(cluster)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `cluster` | string | sim | Cluster identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cluster-01") or a full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_clusters. Must resolve to exactly one cluster. |

#### `vmware_cluster_stamp_all_rules_with_uuid`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Stamp a UUID onto every VM/host affinity/anti-affinity rule in a cluster's configuration that does not already have one — an internal bookkeeping/migration operation, not a behavioral rule change.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_cluster_stamp_all_rules_with_uuid(cluster, confirm)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `cluster` | string | sim | Cluster identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cluster-01") or a full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_clusters. Must resolve to exactly one cluster. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |

Must resolve to exactly one compute resource (cluster or standalone host). |

#### `vmware_compute_resource_environment_browser`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `compute_resource` | string | sim | ComputeResource identifier: a cluster's name/pattern (e.g. "cluster-01"), a standalone ESXi host's own name (its implicit compute resource, e.g. "esxi-01.local"), or a full inventory path under the datacenter's host folder. Must resolve to exactly one compute resource (cluster or standalone host). |

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `compute_resource` | string | sim | ComputeResource identifier: a cluster's name/pattern (e.g. "cluster-01"), a standalone ESXi host's own name (its implicit compute resource, e.g. "esxi-01.local"), or a full inventory path under the datacenter's host folder. Must resolve to exactly one compute resource (cluster or standalone host). |

#### `vmware_compute_resource_reconfigure`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Reconfigure a compute resource's swapfile placement / SPBM / cluster (DRS, HA, VSAN, rules, groups) settings. Accepts a types.ClusterConfigSpecEx as spec — see this file's top doc comment for why this is used instead of the base types.ComputeResourceConfigSpec: real vCenter/govc practice and vcsim's own simulator both require the richer ClusterConfigSpecEx shape, which is also a valid types.BaseComputeResourceConfigSpec implementer. Only meaningful against an actual cluster — vcsim (and likely real vSphere) has no server-side handler for this on a plain standalone host's implicit compute resource.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_compute_resource_reconfigure(compute_resource, confirm, spec, [modify])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `compute_resource` | string | sim | ComputeResource identifier: a cluster's name/pattern (e.g. "cluster-01"), a standalone ESXi host's own name (its implicit compute resource, e.g. "esxi-01.local"), or a full inventory path under the datacenter's host folder. Must resolve to exactly one compute resource (cluster or standalone host). |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `modify` | boolean | — | true (default) merges spec into the existing configuration; false replaces it wholesale. |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.ClusterConfigSpecEx JSON object matching its Go struct fields (drsConfig, dasConfig, vsanConfig, rulesSpec, groupSpec, etc.). |

#### `vmware_compute_resource_resource_pool`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Get the root resource pool of a compute resource — every ComputeResource/ClusterComputeResource has at least an implicit "Resources" pool.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_compute_resource_resource_pool(compute_resource)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `compute_resource` | string | sim | ComputeResource identifier: a cluster's name/pattern (e.g. "cluster-01"), a standalone ESXi host's own name (its implicit compute resource, e.g. "esxi-01.local"), or a full inventory path under the datacenter's host folder. Must resolve to exactly one compute resource (cluster or standalone host). |

### Criptografia / KMS (30)

#### `vmware_crypto_add_key`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Add one already-existing raw cryptographic key (bring-your-own-key material) to vCenter's key management.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_crypto_add_key(algorithm, confirm, key_data, key_id, [provider_id])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `algorithm` | string | sim | Key algorithm, e.g. "AES-256". |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `key_data` | string | sim | The raw key material (CryptoKeyPlain.keyData) — sensitive; handle like a secret. |
| `key_id` | string | sim | The cryptographic key's ID (CryptoKeyId.keyId). |
| `provider_id` | string | — | Optional: the KMS provider (KeyProviderId.Id) holding this key's data, if known/different from the default. |

#### `vmware_crypto_add_keys`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Add multiple already-existing raw cryptographic keys in one call. "keys" is a JSON array of objects shaped like govmomi's CryptoKeyPlain: {"keyId":{"keyId":"...","providerId":{"id":"..."}?},"algorithm":"...","keyData":"..."}.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_crypto_add_keys(confirm, keys)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `keys` | array&lt;object&gt; | sim | Non-empty array of CryptoKeyPlain-shaped objects — see tool description. |

#### `vmware_crypto_generate_client_csr`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Generate a certificate signing request (CSR) for vCenter's KMIP client certificate against a given cluster, without persisting/uploading anything.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_crypto_generate_client_csr(cluster_id, [request])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `cluster_id` | string | sim | KMIP cluster / KMS provider ID (KeyProviderId.Id) — e.g. as returned by vmware_crypto_list_kmip_servers' kmip_servers[].clusterId.id. |
| `request` | object | — | Optional certificate sign request fields, shaped like govmomi's CryptoManagerKmipCertSignRequest: {"commonName"?,"organization"?,"organizationUnit"?,"locality"?,"state"?,"country"?,"email"?}. All fields optional; omit for a request with no distinguished-name fields set. |

#### `vmware_crypto_generate_key`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Generate a new cryptographic key at a KMS provider (native or KMIP-backed). Reversible via vmware_crypto_remove_key.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_crypto_generate_key(confirm, [attributes, cluster_id, key_type])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `attributes` | array&lt;object&gt; | — | Optional custom key attributes, as an array of {"key":"...","value":"..."} objects. |
| `cluster_id` | string | — | KMS provider to generate the key at. Omit to use the default provider. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `key_type` | string | — | Requested key type (KmipClusterInfoKeyType_enum: "rawKey" or "wrappedKey"). Omit to use the provider's default key type. |

#### `vmware_crypto_generate_self_signed_client_cert`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Generate (and adopt as) a new self-signed client certificate for vCenter's KMIP client identity against a given cluster. Reversible by generating another, but replaces the certificate KMIP servers currently trust for this client.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_crypto_generate_self_signed_client_cert(cluster_id, confirm, [request])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `cluster_id` | string | sim | KMIP cluster / KMS provider ID (KeyProviderId.Id) — e.g. as returned by vmware_crypto_list_kmip_servers' kmip_servers[].clusterId.id. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `request` | object | — | Optional certificate sign request fields, shaped like govmomi's CryptoManagerKmipCertSignRequest: {"commonName"?,"organization"?,"organizationUnit"?,"locality"?,"state"?,"country"?,"email"?}. All fields optional; omit for a request with no distinguished-name fields set. |

#### `vmware_crypto_get_default_kms_cluster`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Get the default KMS/KMIP cluster used for encryption — the connection-wide global default, or the default for a specific entity (host folder/cluster) if entity_path is given.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_crypto_get_default_kms_cluster([entity_path, follow_parent_hierarchy])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `entity_path` | string | — | Optional inventory path of the ManagedEntity this default applies to (currently cluster or host folder per the vSphere API), e.g. "/DC0/host/Cluster1". Omit for the connection-wide global default. |
| `follow_parent_hierarchy` | boolean | — | If true and entity_path has no default of its own, walk up to its parent's default instead of returning none. Defaults to false. |

#### `vmware_crypto_is_kms_cluster_active`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Check whether a KMS/KMIP cluster (or the default cluster, if cluster_id is omitted) is currently active.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_crypto_is_kms_cluster_active([cluster_id])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `cluster_id` | string | — | Optional KMIP cluster / KMS provider ID (KeyProviderId.Id). Where supported, omitting this uses the default cluster/provider instead of a specific one. |

#### `vmware_crypto_kms_provider_create`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Register a new KMS (Key Management Server) provider for vSphere VM encryption.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_crypto_kms_provider_create(confirm, provider, [tpm_required])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |

| `provider` | string | sim | Identifier of the KMS provider (as configured in vCenter's native key provider / KMIP cluster configuration). |

Remove a registered KMS provider. Irreversible — any VMs still encrypted with keys from this provider become inaccessible unless the provider (or its keys) can be restored independently.

| `provider` | string | sim | Identifier of the KMS provider (as configured in vCenter's native key provider / KMIP cluster configuration). |

#### `vmware_crypto_kms_provider_export`

Export a KMS provider's configuration (a downloadable location + one-time download token — see .location in the result), e.g. to re-import it as a trusted provider elsewhere.

| `password` | string | — | Optional password protecting the exported configuration, if the KMS plugin supports/requires one. |
| `provider` | string | sim | Identifier of the KMS provider (as configured in vCenter's native key provider / KMIP cluster configuration). |

List cryptographic key IDs known to vCenter's key management (across registered KMS providers), optionally capped by limit.

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Mark a KMS cluster as the connection-wide global default (shorthand for vmware_crypto_set_default_kms_cluster with no entity_path).

#### `vmware_crypto_query_key_status`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Check the availability of one or more cryptographic keys, and optionally which VMs/hosts are using them. "key_ids" is a JSON array of objects shaped like govmomi's CryptoKeyId: {"keyId":"...","providerId":{"id":"..."}?}.

| `check_used_by_vms` | boolean | — | Also report which VMs are using each key. Defaults to false. |

#### `vmware_crypto_register_kmip_server`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Register a new KMIP server (KMS) under a cluster ID. If the cluster ID doesn't exist yet, this creates it as a new externally-managed KMS cluster.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_crypto_register_kmip_server(cluster_id, confirm, server_info, [default_key_type, password])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |

| `cluster_id` | string | sim | KMIP cluster / KMS provider ID (KeyProviderId.Id) — e.g. as returned by vmware_crypto_list_kmip_servers' kmip_servers[].clusterId.id. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `default_key_type` | string | — | Key type this provider generates by default (KmipClusterInfoKeyType_enum: "rawKey" or "wrappedKey"). Optional. |
| `password` | string | — | Password to authenticate to the KMIP server. Set to an empty string to clear a previously-set password. |
| `server_info` | object | sim | KMIP server connection info, shaped like govmomi's KmipServerInfo (govmomi field names, not snake_case): {"name":"...","address":"...","port":5696,"proxyAddress"?,"proxyPort"?,"reconnect"?,"protocol"?,"nbio"?,"timeout"?,"userName"?}. "name" is required. |

#### `vmware_crypto_register_kms_cluster`

Register a new, empty KMS cluster ID with a management type (before adding KMIP servers to it via vmware_crypto_register_kmip_server).

| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `management_type` | string | — | Key provider management type (KmipClusterInfoKmsManagementType_enum: "unknown", "vCenter", "trustAuthority", or "nativeProvider"). Defaults to "trustAuthority" per the vSphere API if omitted — pass it explicitly against a vcsim/test target, which does not apply that default itself. |

#### `vmware_crypto_remove_key`

| `key_id` | string | sim | The cryptographic key's ID (CryptoKeyId.keyId). |
| `provider_id` | string | — | Optional: the KMS provider (KeyProviderId.Id) holding this key's data, if known/different from the default. |

#### `vmware_crypto_remove_keys`

| `force` | boolean | — | Remove keys even if in use. Always successful for keys that exist. Defaults to false. |
| `keys` | array&lt;object&gt; | sim | Non-empty array of CryptoKeyId-shaped objects — see tool description. |

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Set (or clear, by omitting cluster_id) the default KMS cluster — globally, or scoped to a specific entity (host folder/cluster) via entity_path.

### Customization Spec (10)

#### `vmware_customization_spec_create`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new customization spec. Fails if a spec with the same name already exists — use vmware_customization_spec_overwrite to replace an existing one.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_customization_spec_create(confirm, item)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `item` | object | sim | A types.CustomizationSpecItem JSON object matching its Go struct field names: "info" (types.CustomizationSpecInfo: "name" required unique string, plus "description"/"type" strings) and "spec" (types.CustomizationSpec). IMPORTANT LIMITATION (see this file's top doc comment): "spec.identity" and "spec.options" are polymorphic fields (6 possible Identity variants, 2 possible Options variants) that this tool's generic JSON decode cannot populate — omit both (leave "spec" with only e.g. "globalIPSettings":{} and "nicSettingMap":[]) or the call fails with a clear decode error naming the offending field. "spec.globalIPSettings" and "spec.nicSettingMap" are ordinary concrete structs and decode normally. See referencia/govmomi/vim25/types/types.go's CustomizationSpecItem/CustomizationSpec for the full field list. |

| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `name` | string | sim | Unique name of a customization spec, e.g. "vcsim-linux" (vcsim's own built-in default) or any name returned by vmware_customization_spec_info. |

### Datacenter (7)

#### `vmware_datacenter_destroy`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Permanently delete a datacenter and everything in it. Irreversible. Fails with ResourceInUse if the datacenter's vm/host folders still contain anything — empty them first.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_datacenter_destroy(confirm, datacenter)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `datacenter` | string | sim | Datacenter identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "DC0") or a full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. Must resolve to exactly one datacenter. |

#### `vmware_datacenter_folders`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Get the 4 well-known inventory sub-folders of a datacenter (vm/host/datastore/network) with their resolved inventory paths.

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `datacenter` | string | sim | Datacenter identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "DC0") or a full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. Must resolve to exactly one datacenter. |

#### `vmware_datacenter_power_on_vm`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Power on multiple virtual machines in a datacenter with a single call (more efficient than calling vmware_vm_power_on once per VM against vCenter). Against a standalone ESXi host, VMs are powered on serially instead (no batching available) — reported the same way.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_datacenter_power_on_vm(confirm, datacenter, vms, [option])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `datacenter` | string | sim | Datacenter identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "DC0") or a full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. Must resolve to exactly one datacenter. |
| `option` | array&lt;object&gt; | — | Optional array of types.OptionValue JSON objects ({"key":"...","value":"..."}) — low-level power-on options. Omit in the common case. |
| `vms` | array&lt;string&gt; | sim | VM identifiers by name/pattern (see vmware_list_vms), each resolved to exactly one VM. Non-empty, required. |

#### `vmware_datacenter_query_connection_info`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Probe whether a host (by hostname/port/credentials) can be added to this datacenter, without adding it — returns the host's summary, VM list, and whether it's already managed by another vCenter. Performs a real network connection to the target host to answer the question; does not modify inventory.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_datacenter_query_connection_info(datacenter, hostname, password, port, username, [ssl_certificate, ssl_thumbprint])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `datacenter` | string | sim | Datacenter identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "DC0") or a full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. Must resolve to exactly one datacenter. |
| `hostname` | string | sim | Target host's hostname or IP address. Required. |
| `password` | string | sim | Password to authenticate against the target host. Required. |
| `port` | integer | sim | Target port. ESX 3.x+/VMware Server hosts use the https port (443 by default); pass -1 to let the server try the default. Required. |
| `ssl_certificate` | string | — | Optional expected SSL certificate of the host in PEM format — a fallback when ssl_thumbprint can't be verified via a trusted CA. Mutually exclusive with ssl_thumbprint. |
| `ssl_thumbprint` | string | — | Optional expected SSL thumbprint of the host's certificate. |
| `username` | string | sim | Username to authenticate against the target host. Required. |

#### `vmware_datacenter_query_connection_info_via_spec`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Same probe as vmware_datacenter_query_connection_info_via_spec's sibling vmware_datacenter_query_connection_info, but driven by a full HostConnectSpec instead of separate hostname/port/username/password arguments.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_datacenter_query_connection_info_via_spec(datacenter, spec)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `datacenter` | string | sim | Datacenter identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "DC0") or a full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. Must resolve to exactly one datacenter. |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.HostConnectSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields — "hostName"/"userName"/"password" are required for a real connection attempt to succeed. Required. |

|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `datacenter` | string | sim | Datacenter identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "DC0") or a full inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. Must resolve to exactly one datacenter. |
| `modify` | boolean | — | If true (default false), spec is applied incrementally (unset fields keep their current value); if false, the datacenter's config matches spec exactly (unset fields reset to default). |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.DatacenterConfigSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields — "defaultHardwareVersionKey"/"maximumHardwareVersionKey" (both optional strings, e.g. "vmx-19"; see vmware_datacenter_query_config_option_descriptor's "key" field for valid values). Required. |

#### `vmware_datastore_download_file`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Download a file from a path inside a vSphere datastore to the filesystem of the machine running this MCP server. local_path is written on this server's own filesystem — NOT streamed back to the MCP client/chat — and is silently overwritten if it already exists (govmomi's own download implementation has no overwrite guard, unlike this project's vmware_datastore_upload_file for the remote side).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_datastore_download_file(confirm, datastore, local_path, remote_path)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `datastore` | string | sim | Datastore name/pattern (e.g. "datastore1") as returned by vmware_list_datastores. Must resolve to exactly one datastore. |
| `local_path` | string | sim | Destination path on the machine running this MCP server. Overwritten if it already exists. |
| `remote_path` | string | sim | Source path inside the datastore, e.g. "ISOs/ubuntu-24.04.iso". |

#### `vmware_datastore_file_copy`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Copy a file on a datastore. If the source path ends in ".vmdk" this dispatches to the virtual-disk-aware copy (also copies the matching "-flat.vmdk" backing extent) instead of a plain byte copy — see vmware_datastore_file_copy_file for the always-plain-byte-copy variant, which would leave a .vmdk copy broken. Fails if destination already exists unless force:true.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_datastore_file_copy(confirm, datastore, destination, source, [force])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `datastore` | string | sim | Datastore name/pattern (e.g. "datastore1") as returned by vmware_list_datastores. Must resolve to exactly one datastore — its owning Datacenter is derived automatically from it, no separate datacenter argument needed. |
| `destination` | string | sim | Path to the destination file, relative to "datastore" (e.g. "ISOs/old.iso"), or a full bracketed datastore path (e.g. "[datastore2] ISOs/old.iso") to reach a DIFFERENT datastore than "datastore" — same datacenter only (see this file's top doc comment). |
| `force` | boolean | — | Copy/move tools: overwrite an existing destination file instead of failing. vmware_datastore_file_delete_virtual_disk only: best-effort clear the virtual disk's ddb.deletable=false flag before deleting it. Default false in both cases. |
| `source` | string | sim | Path to the source file, relative to "datastore" (e.g. "ISOs/old.iso"), or a full bracketed datastore path (e.g. "[datastore2] ISOs/old.iso") to reach a DIFFERENT datastore than "datastore" — same datacenter only (see this file's top doc comment). |

#### `vmware_datastore_file_copy_file`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Copy a file on a datastore as a plain byte-for-byte copy, even if the source is a ".vmdk" descriptor — in that case the "-flat.vmdk" backing extent is NOT copied, producing an unusable/incomplete virtual disk at the destination. Use vmware_datastore_file_copy instead for anything that might be a virtual disk. Fails if destination already exists unless force:true.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_datastore_file_copy_file(confirm, datastore, destination, source, [force])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |

| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |

| `destination` | string | sim | Path to the destination file, relative to "datastore" (e.g. "ISOs/old.iso"), or a full bracketed datastore path (e.g. "[datastore2] ISOs/old.iso") to reach a DIFFERENT datastore than "datastore" — same datacenter only (see this file's top doc comment). |
| `force` | boolean | — | Copy/move tools: overwrite an existing destination file instead of failing. vmware_datastore_file_delete_virtual_disk only: best-effort clear the virtual disk's ddb.deletable=false flag before deleting it. Default false in both cases. |
| `source` | string | sim | Path to the source file, relative to "datastore" (e.g. "ISOs/old.iso"), or a full bracketed datastore path (e.g. "[datastore2] ISOs/old.iso") to reach a DIFFERENT datastore than "datastore" — same datacenter only (see this file's top doc comment). |

| `name` | string | sim | Path to the target file, relative to "datastore" (e.g. "ISOs/old.iso"), or a full bracketed datastore path (e.g. "[datastore2] ISOs/old.iso") to reach a DIFFERENT datastore than "datastore" — same datacenter only (see this file's top doc comment). |

#### `vmware_datastore_file_delete_virtual_disk`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Delete a virtual disk (".vmdk" descriptor + its "-flat.vmdk" backing extent) on a datastore, with the Datacenter derived automatically from "datastore" — no separate datacenter argument needed. | `name` | string | sim | Path to the target file, relative to "datastore" (e.g. "ISOs/old.iso"), or a full bracketed datastore path (e.g. "[datastore2] ISOs/old.iso") to reach a DIFFERENT datastore than "datastore" — same datacenter only (see this file's top doc comment). |

#### `vmware_datastore_open`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Read up to max_bytes of a file's contents from a datastore, starting at an optional byte offset, and return them base64-encoded. Not a full file transfer — use vmware_datastore_download_file to save a complete file to this server's local disk. max_bytes defaults to 65536 (64KiB) and is capped at 10485760 (10MiB) server-side regardless of what is requested; the response's "truncated" field reports whether more data remained beyond the returned chunk.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_datastore_open(confirm, datastore, remote_path, [max_bytes, offset])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `datastore` | string | sim | Datastore name/pattern (e.g. "datastore1") as returned by vmware_list_datastores. Must resolve to exactly one datastore. |
| `max_bytes` | integer | — | Maximum number of bytes to read. Default 65536 (64KiB); capped at 10485760 (10MiB). |
| `offset` | integer | — | Byte offset to start reading from. Default 0 (start of file). |
| `remote_path` | string | sim | Path to the file within the datastore, e.g. "logs/vmware.log". |

#### `vmware_datastore_search`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Search a single folder on a datastore for files matching a search spec (non-recursive — use vmware_datastore_search_subfolders to also search subfolders).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_datastore_search(datastore, path, [search_spec])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `datastore` | string | sim | Datastore name/pattern (e.g. "datastore1") as returned by vmware_list_datastores. Must resolve to exactly one datastore. |
| `path` | string | sim | Folder within the datastore to search, e.g. "ISOs" or "" for the datastore root. |
| `search_spec` | object | — | A types.HostDatastoreBrowserSearchSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields ("matchPattern" glob list, "query" file-type filter list, "details" flags for size/owner/modification/type, "searchCaseInsensitive"). Omit to match every file under path (matchPattern defaults to ["*"]). |

Omit to match every file under path (matchPattern defaults to ["*"]). |

Upload a file (e.g. an ISO) to a path inside a vSphere datastore. local_path is read from the filesystem of the machine running this MCP server — NOT uploaded from the MCP client/chat. Refuses to overwrite an existing file at remote_path unless overwrite:true.

| `overwrite` | boolean | — | Allow replacing an existing file at remote_path. Default false — the upload is refused if a file already exists there. |
| `remote_path` | string | sim | Destination path inside the datastore, e.g. "ISOs/ubuntu-24.04.iso". Parent folders are created automatically if missing. |

#### `vmware_diagnostic_browse_log`

Read a slice of lines from a diagnostic log (e.g. vpxd, hostd) by key, starting at a given line. Use vmware_diagnostic_query_descriptions to discover valid log keys.

| `host` | string | — | Host identifier (see vmware_list_hosts). Optional — omit to target vCenter's own log (vpxd) instead of a specific ESXi host's. |
| `key` | string | sim | Log identifier, e.g. "hostd" or "vpxd" (see vmware_diagnostic_query_descriptions). |
| `lines` | integer | — | Maximum number of lines to return. Default 0 (server default, typically returns just the header/no text). |
| `start` | integer | — | Line number to start reading from. Default 0 (start of log). |

#### `vmware_diagnostic_generate_log_bundles`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Generate a support log bundle for vCenter and/or one or more ESXi hosts. Blocks until the underlying task completes; the download URL(s) for the generated bundle(s) are NOT returned by this tool (see this file's top doc comment) — this only confirms the bundle(s) were generated.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_diagnostic_generate_log_bundles(confirm, [hosts, include_default])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `hosts` | array&lt;string&gt; | — | Host identifiers to include (see vmware_list_hosts). Omit for none (only meaningful combined with include_default:true, or against a standalone ESXi host). |
| `include_default` | boolean | — | Include the default log bundle (vCenter Server's own logs) in addition to any hosts listed. Default false. |

#### `vmware_diagnostic_log_copy`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Read (a bounded amount of) a diagnostic log's text content, optionally starting from only the last tail_lines lines. See this file's top doc comment for why this is Tier 2 despite being a read.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_diagnostic_log_copy(confirm, log_key, [host, max_bytes, tail_lines])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host` | string | — | Host identifier (see vmware_list_hosts). Optional — omit to target vCenter's own log (vpxd) instead of a specific ESXi host's. |
| `log_key` | string | sim | Log identifier, e.g. "hostd" or "vpxd" (see vmware_diagnostic_query_descriptions). |
| `max_bytes` | integer | — | Maximum number of bytes of log text to return. Default 2097152 (2MiB); hard-capped server-side regardless of what is requested. |
| `tail_lines` | integer | — | If given, seek to only the last N lines of the log before copying, instead of starting from the beginning. |

#### `vmware_diagnostic_query_descriptions`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List the diagnostic log keys available on vCenter or a specific ESXi host, with their descriptions.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_diagnostic_query_descriptions([host])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `host` | string | — | Host identifier (see vmware_list_hosts). Optional — omit to target vCenter's own log (vpxd) instead of a specific ESXi host's. |

#### `vmware_dvsmgr_export_entity`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Export the configuration of one or more Distributed Virtual Switches/Portgroups as an opaque backup blob, for later restore via vmware_dvs_rollback or vmware_dvsmgr_import_entity. Read-only (does not modify any switch) despite being a *_Task method — see generated_dvs.go's top doc comment.

| `import_type` | string | sim | How to apply the backup — see EntityImportType_enum (e.g. "createEntityWithNewIdentifier", "createEntityWithOriginalIdentifier", "applyToEntitySpecified"). |

### ESX Settings (cluster VMs) (16)

#### `vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_apply`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Apply the current desired solution specification(s) to a cluster and return a task ID (feed it into vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_apply_wait_for_completion, or vmware_cis_tasks_wait_for_completion, to poll it). Does not itself block on the task.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_apply(cluster_path, confirm, [apply_spec])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `apply_spec` | object | — | Optional ApplySpec JSON object narrowing which solutions/hosts to apply: {"host_solutions": {"solutions": [...], "hosts": [...]}, "cluster_solutions": {"solutions": [...], "hosts": [...]}} (both filters optional; omitted/empty on both means "apply everything on the cluster"). |
| `cluster_path` | string | sim | Full inventory path of the target ClusterComputeResource (e.g. "/DC0/host/cluster1"), resolved via SearchIndex.FindByInventoryPath. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |

#### `vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_apply_wait_for_completion`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Block until an apply task (started by vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_apply) completes, and return its ApplyResult. timeout_seconds is REQUIRED (no default) — this polls a REST task with no server-side timeout of its own.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_apply_wait_for_completion(confirm, task_id, timeout_seconds)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `task_id` | string | sim | Task ID returned by vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_apply. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | sim | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever. REQUIRED — no default — this call polls a REST endpoint with no server-side timeout of its own. |

#### `vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_check_compliance`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Check compliance of a cluster's System VM deployments against their desired solution specifications. Blocks until the underlying task completes (bounded by timeout_seconds, default 300s) — despite being a read/check operation, this is registered as tier2 exactly as classified by the codegen brief for this group (kept as specified, not independently 'corrected' — see this file's top doc comment).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_check_compliance(cluster_path, confirm, [filter_spec, timeout_seconds])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `cluster_path` | string | sim | Full inventory path of the target ClusterComputeResource (e.g. "/DC0/host/cluster1"), resolved via SearchIndex.FindByInventoryPath. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `filter_spec` | object | — | Optional CheckComplianceFilterSpec JSON object narrowing the check: {"solutions": [...], "hosts": [...], "deployment_units": [...]} (all optional; omitted/empty means "check everything in the cluster"). |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | — | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever — this call polls a REST task with no server-side timeout of its own (see this file's top doc comment). Default 300 (5 minutes) if omitted. |

#### `vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_delete_solution`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Delete a solution's desired specification for a cluster outright. Irreversible — distinct from vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_delete_solution_only, which only marks System VMs for abandonment on the next apply (see this file's top doc comment). Blocks until the underlying task completes (bounded by timeout_seconds, default 300s).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_esx_settings_clusters_vms_delete_solution(cluster_path, confirm, solution, [timeout_seconds])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |

| `cluster_path` | string | sim | Full inventory path of the target ClusterComputeResource (e.g. "/DC0/host/cluster1"), resolved via SearchIndex.FindByInventoryPath. |

| `solution` | string | sim | Identifier of the vLCM System VM Solution within the cluster (e.g. an EAM agency ID, or a caller-defined identifier used consistently across Set/Get/Delete/Enable/Transition calls for it). |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | — | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever — this call polls a REST task with no server-side timeout of its own (see this file's top doc comment). Default 300 (5 minutes) if omitted. |

Key fields: deployment_type ("EVERY_HOST_PINNED"\|"CLUSTER_VM_SET"), display_name, display_version, vm_name_template ({prefix, suffix: "UUID"\|"COUNTER"}), cluster_solution_spec (only for CLUSTER_VM_SET: vm_count, vm_placement_policies, vm_networks, vm_datastores, devices, remediation_policy, alternative_vm_specs), hook_configurations (map of "POST_PROVISIONING"/"POST_POWER_ON" -> {timeout}), ovf_resource ({location_type, url, ssl_certificate_validation, certificate, authentication_scheme}), ovf_descriptor_properties, vm_clone_config, vm_storage_policy, vm_storage_profiles, vm_disk_type, vm_resource_pool, vm_folder, vm_resource_spec, redeployment_policy. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | — | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever — this call polls a REST task with no server-side timeout of its own (see this file's top doc comment). Default 300 (5 minutes) if omitted. |

### Eventos (5)

#### `vmware_event_create_collector`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a server-side EventHistoryCollector scoped to a filter, for paged/incremental event retrieval. Reversible in the sense that the collector is a disposable server-side resource (there is a per-vCenter cap on how many can exist at once — MaxCollector); this project has no separate tool yet to read pages from or destroy the returned collector — the moref is returned for advanced/future use.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_event_create_collector(confirm, filter)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `filter` | object | sim | Optional types.EventFilterSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields — all fields optional, an empty/omitted filter matches every visible event. "entity": {"entity":{"type":"...","value":"..."},"recursion":"self"\|"children"\|"all"}. "time": {"beginTime":"RFC3339","endTime":"RFC3339"}. "userName": {"userList":["..."],"systemUser":bool}. "eventChainId": int32. "alarm"/"scheduledTask": {"type":"Alarm"\|"ScheduledTask","value":"..."}. "category": array of severity strings ("info"\|"warning"\|"error"\|"user"). "eventTypeId": array of event type-id strings (e.g. "VmPoweredOnEvent", or a custom EventEx eventTypeId). "maxCount": int32 cap on returned events. Required (may be an empty object {} to match every event). |

#### `vmware_event_log_user_event`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Log a simple user-defined event (just a message string) against an entity. For a fully custom event with its own type id/severity/arguments, use vmware_event_post instead.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_event_log_user_event(confirm, msg, [entity, host, vm])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `entity` | object | — | Explicit MoRef of the target managed object/entity, e.g. {"type": "ClusterComputeResource", "value": "domain-c7"} — use this to target a kind vmware_list_vms/vmware_list_hosts can't resolve directly (cluster, datacenter, resource pool, datastore, network, folder, vApp...). Alternative to "vm"/"host". |
| `host` | string | — | Host identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Alternative to "entity"/"vm". |
| `msg` | string | sim | The message to log. Required. |
| `vm` | string | — | VM identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_vms. Alternative to "entity"/"host". |

#### `vmware_event_post`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Post a fully custom event (types.EventEx) into vCenter/ESXi's event history — visible to vmware_event_query, alarms, and any other event consumer.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_event_post(confirm, event)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `event` | object | sim | A types.EventEx JSON object matching its Go struct fields — "eventTypeId" (string, required) identifies the custom event type; "message" (string), "severity" ("info"\|"warning"\|"error"\|"user", default info), "arguments" (array of {"key":"...","value":"..."}), "objectId"/"objectType"/"objectName" (the affected object, e.g. objectType:"VirtualMachine"). Server-managed fields (key/chainId/createdTime/userName) are ignored if set — the server assigns real values on post. The full range of predefined vSphere event types (VmPoweredOnEvent, etc.) is NOT supported here — EventEx is the one generic/custom vehicle this tool exposes. |

#### `vmware_event_query`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Query the event history for events matching a filter (by entity/time/user/category/type). One-shot — returns the latest page of matches directly, no separate collector object to manage (use vmware_event_create_collector for paged/live collection instead).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_event_query([filter])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `filter` | object | — | Optional types.EventFilterSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields — all fields optional, an empty/omitted filter matches every visible event. "entity": {"entity":{"type":"...","value":"..."},"recursion":"self"\|"children"\|"all"}. "time": {"beginTime":"RFC3339","endTime":"RFC3339"}. "userName": {"userList":["..."],"systemUser":bool}. "eventChainId": int32. "alarm"/"scheduledTask": {"type":"Alarm"\|"ScheduledTask","value":"..."}. "category": array of severity strings ("info"\|"warning"\|"error"\|"user"). "eventTypeId": array of event type-id strings (e.g. "VmPoweredOnEvent", or a custom EventEx eventTypeId). "maxCount": int32 cap on returned events. |

#### `vmware_event_retrieve_argument_description`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Get the argument descriptions (name/type per positional argument) for a given event type id — useful to interpret an EventEx/ExtendedEvent's raw Arguments array.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_event_retrieve_argument_description(event_type_id)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `event_type_id` | string | sim | The event type id, e.g. "com.vmware.applmgmt.MyEvent" or a predefined event class name like "VmPoweredOnEvent". Required. |

### Extension Manager (6)

#### `vmware_extension_find`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Look up a single registered vCenter extension (a plugin/solution registration, e.g. from the Solutions/Client Plug-Ins inventory) by its key. Reports {"found": false} instead of an error if no extension with that key is registered.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_extension_find(key)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `key` | string | sim | Extension key (Java-package-style unique identifier, e.g. "com.example.myplugin"), as returned by vmware_extension_list or vmware_extension_find. |

#### `vmware_extension_list`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

List every vCenter extension (plugin/solution) registered on this connection.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_extension_list()`

_Sem parametros._

#### `vmware_extension_register`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Register a new vCenter extension (plugin/solution). Fails if an extension with the same key is already registered — use vmware_extension_update to modify an existing one.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_extension_register(confirm, extension)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `extension` | object | sim | A types.Extension JSON object matching its Go struct field names. "key" (string, Java-package-style unique identifier, e.g. "com.example.myplugin") and "version" (dot-separated string, e.g. "1.0.0") are effectively required by the real API/vCenter UI even though vcsim itself only rejects a duplicate "key". Common optional fields: "company", "type", "subjectName". "description", if supplied, must be {"label":"...","summary":"..."} — the one concrete shape this tool's decode supports for that field (see this file's top doc comment). See referencia/govmomi/vim25/types/types.go's Extension struct for the full field list (server/client/task/event/fault/privilege/resource lists are accepted as-is if supplied, but are rarely needed for a basic registration). |

#### `vmware_extension_set_certificate`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Set (replace) the client certificate (PEM-encoded) associated with an already-registered extension, used to authenticate that extension via LoginExtensionByCertificate.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_extension_set_certificate(certificate_pem, confirm, key)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `certificate_pem` | string | sim | PEM-encoded X.509 certificate to associate with the extension. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `key` | string | sim | Extension key (Java-package-style unique identifier, e.g. "com.example.myplugin"), as returned by vmware_extension_list or vmware_extension_find. |

#### `vmware_extension_unregister`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Permanently remove a vCenter extension (plugin/solution) registration. Irreversible (the registration itself, and any client-side certificate association, is gone — re-registering starts fresh).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_extension_unregister(confirm, key)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `key` | string | sim | Extension key (Java-package-style unique identifier, e.g. "com.example.myplugin"), as returned by vmware_extension_list or vmware_extension_find. |

#### `vmware_extension_update`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Update (overwrite) the registration of an already-registered vCenter extension. Fails if no extension with the given key is registered — use vmware_extension_register to create a new one.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_extension_update(confirm, extension)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `extension` | object | sim | A types.Extension JSON object matching its Go struct field names. "key" (string, Java-package-style unique identifier, e.g. "com.example.myplugin") and "version" (dot-separated string, e.g. "1.0.0") are effectively required by the real API/vCenter UI even though vcsim itself only rejects a duplicate "key". Common optional fields: "company", "type", "subjectName". "description", if supplied, must be {"label":"...","summary":"..."} — the one concrete shape this tool's decode supports for that field (see this file's top doc comment). See referencia/govmomi/vim25/types/types.go's Extension struct for the full field list (server/client/task/event/fault/privilege/resource lists are accepted as-is if supplied, but are rarely needed for a basic registration). |
