#### `vmware_fcd_clone`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Clone a First Class Disk into a new one on a (possibly different) datastore. Not simulated by this project's test harness (vcsim has no CloneVStorageObject_Task handler) — exercise carefully against a real vCenter first. Reversible via vmware_fcd_delete on the clone.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_fcd_clone(confirm, datastore, dest_datastore, id, name, [dest_path, keep_after_delete_vm, provisioning_type])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |

| `dest_datastore` | string | sim | Destination datastore name/pattern for the clone's backing file. May be the same as datastore. |
| `dest_path` | string | — | Relative path within dest_datastore for the clone's disk file. Optional — omit for the server default FCD location. |

| `name` | string | sim | Descriptive name for the cloned virtual storage object. |
| `provisioning_type` | string | — | Provisioning type for the clone's backing, e.g. "thin", "eagerZeroedThick", "lazyZeroedThick". Optional. |

### Datastore - Arquivos (4)

#### `vmware_file_copy_datastore_file`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Copy a file between datastore paths, each independently scoped to its own Datacenter — unlike vmware_datastore_file_copy_file (which derives a single Datacenter from one "datastore" argument), this supports a genuinely cross-datacenter copy. Path arguments must be full bracketed datastore paths, e.g. "[datastore1] ISOs/old.iso". Fails if destination already exists unless force:true.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_file_copy_datastore_file(confirm, destination_datacenter, destination_path, source_datacenter, source_path, [force])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `destination_datacenter` | string | sim | Datacenter name/pattern (e.g. "DC0") as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. Must resolve to exactly one datacenter. |
| `destination_path` | string | sim | Full bracketed datastore path, e.g. "[datastore1] ISOs/old.iso" — required here (unlike the vmware_datastore_file_* tools above) because this tool has no "datastore" argument of its own to auto-derive a Datacenter from. |
| `force` | boolean | — | Overwrite an existing destination file instead of failing. Default false. |
| `source_datacenter` | string | sim | Datacenter name/pattern (e.g. "DC0") as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. Must resolve to exactly one datacenter. |
| `source_path` | string | sim | Full bracketed datastore path, e.g. "[datastore1] ISOs/old.iso" — required here (unlike the vmware_datastore_file_* tools above) because this tool has no "datastore" argument of its own to auto-derive a Datacenter from. |

#### `vmware_file_make_directory`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a folder at a datastore path. This is the SAME underlying FileManager.MakeDirectory call tools/datastore.go already uses internally inside vmware_datastore_upload_file (there, best-effort and with errors swallowed, only to auto-create a missing parent folder before an upload) — this tool exposes it directly as its own operation (e.g. pre-create an empty folder without uploading anything) and surfaces real errors instead of swallowing them.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_file_make_directory(confirm, datacenter, path, [create_parent_directories])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `create_parent_directories` | boolean | — | Create any missing parent folders too. Default false — fails if the immediate parent folder doesn't already exist. |
| `datacenter` | string | sim | Datacenter name/pattern (e.g. "DC0") as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. Must resolve to exactly one datacenter. |
| `path` | string | sim | Full bracketed datastore path, e.g. "[datastore1] ISOs/old.iso" — required here (unlike the vmware_datastore_file_* tools above) because this tool has no "datastore" argument of its own to auto-derive a Datacenter from. |

#### `vmware_folder_add_standalone_host`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Add a standalone ESXi host to vCenter's inventory under a folder (must be a datacenter's "host" folder — see this file's top doc comment). No-op/error if called against a standalone ESXi endpoint (adding a host to itself makes no sense).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_folder_add_standalone_host(confirm, folder, spec, [add_connected, comp_res_spec, license])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `add_connected` | boolean | — | Mark the host as connected immediately after adding it. Default false. |
| `comp_res_spec` | object | — | Optional types.ComputeResourceConfigSpec JSON object (the base/common compute-resource config — e.g. vmSwapPlacement) matching its Go struct fields. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `folder` | string | sim | Folder identifier: a name/pattern resolved under each datacenter's "host" folder by default (the usual real-vSphere target for this operation), or an absolute inventory path (starting with "/") to reach any folder directly — see vmware_folder_children. Must resolve to exactly one folder. |
| `license` | string | — | Optional license key to assign to the host. |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.HostConnectSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields — "hostName" is required, "userName"/"password" are required for a real connection attempt to succeed. |

#### `vmware_folder_create_vm`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new virtual machine under a folder from a full config spec. Unlike vmware_vm_reconfigure's narrow num_cpus/memory_mb subset, this accepts the WHOLE types.VirtualMachineConfigSpec as generic JSON — a caller building one from scratch needs to know the real struct field names (e.g. "files":{"vmPathName":"[datastore1]"}).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_folder_create_vm(config, confirm, folder, resource_pool, [host])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `config` | object | sim | A types.VirtualMachineConfigSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields. "name" and "files.vmPathName" (e.g. "[datastore1]") are required by vSphere. Polymorphic sub-fields (e.g. deviceChange) will NOT decode from JSON — omit them and reconfigure devices afterward with a device-management tool. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `folder` | string | sim | Folder identifier: a name/pattern resolved under each datacenter's "vm" folder by default (the usual real-vSphere target for this operation), or an absolute inventory path (starting with "/") to reach any folder directly — see vmware_folder_children. Must resolve to exactly one folder. |
| `host` | string | — | Optional host identifier (see vmware_list_hosts) to place the VM/registration on. Omit to let vSphere pick. |
| `resource_pool` | string | sim | Resource pool name/pattern or full inventory path (e.g. "Resources") as returned by vmware_list_resource_pools. |

Compute (but do not apply) a cross-cluster DRS initial-placement RECOMMENDATION for one or more VMs across a set of resource pools/clusters. Must resolve to exactly one folder. |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.PlaceVmsXClusterSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields — "resourcePools" (array of {"type":"ResourcePool","value":"..."} moref objects, required, non-empty) is the main input; "placementType" defaults to "createAndPowerOn" if omitted. |

### Guest Operations (SO convidado) (26)

#### `vmware_guest_alias_add`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Add a guest alias mapping: let vSphere users authenticated by the given SSO certificate (and, unless subject_type is "any", matching subject_name) impersonate an in-guest user account, inside a VM's guest OS. Reversible via vmware_guest_alias_remove/vmware_guest_alias_remove_by_cert. Requires VMware Tools running in the guest.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_guest_alias_add(base64_cert, confirm, guest_password, guest_username, username, vm, [comment, map_cert, subject_name, subject_type])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `base64_cert` | string | sim | X.509 certificate, in base64-encoded DER format, associated with the alias. |
| `comment` | string | — | Free-form description of the subject, for the operator's own reference. Optional. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `guest_password` | string | sim | Password for guest_username. |
| `guest_username` | string | sim | Username of a valid account inside the guest OS to authenticate the guest operation (this SSO alias-management call itself) as. Not this server's vCenter/ESXi credentials — a separate, guest-OS-local (or domain, if the guest is joined) account. |
| `map_cert` | boolean | — | Map the alias's certificate so future guest operations using it don't need to specify guest_username explicitly. Default false. |
| `subject_name` | string | — | The vSphere subject name (as it appears in the SAML token). Required when subject_type is "named", ignored otherwise. |
| `subject_type` | string | — | The alias subject's kind: "any" (default if omitted) — any vSphere user authenticated by this alias's certificate may impersonate the in-guest user; "named" — only the specific vSphere user given in subject_name may. |
| `username` | string | sim | The in-guest account the alias mapping applies to. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. VMware Tools must be running in its guest OS for any of these tools to succeed. |

Change POSIX ownership/permission attributes of a file inside a VM's guest OS (owner_id/group_id/permissions — any not specified are left unchanged). POSIX guests only. Reversible by setting the previous values back. Requires VMware Tools running in the guest.

| `guest_file_path` | string | sim | Complete path, inside the guest, to the file to change attributes of. If it is a symbolic link, the attributes of the target file are changed. |

| `guest_username` | string | sim | Username of a valid account inside the guest OS to authenticate the guest operation as. Not this server's vCenter/ESXi credentials — a separate, guest-OS-local (or domain, if the guest is joined) account. |
| `owner_id` | integer | — | POSIX owner (user) ID to set on the guest file. Omit to leave unchanged. POSIX guests only. |
| `permissions` | integer | — | POSIX file permissions in chmod(2) numeric form (e.g. 420 decimal = 0644 octal). Omit to leave unchanged. POSIX guests only. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. VMware Tools must be running in its guest OS for any guest-operations tool to succeed. |

| `overwrite` | boolean | — | Clobber the destination file if it already exists. Default false. |

| `permissions` | integer | — | POSIX file permissions in chmod(2) numeric form (e.g. 420 decimal = 0644 octal). Omit to leave unchanged. POSIX guests only. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. VMware Tools must be running in its guest OS for any guest-operations tool to succeed. |

#### `vmware_guest_registry_create_key`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a Windows registry key inside a VM's guest OS. Reversible via vmware_guest_registry_delete_key. Requires VMware Tools running in a Windows guest.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_guest_registry_create_key(confirm, guest_password, guest_username, registry_path, vm, [class_type, is_volatile, wow_bitness])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `class_type` | string | — | User-defined class type for the key. Optional. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `guest_password` | string | sim | Password for guest_username. |
| `guest_username` | string | sim | Username of a valid account inside the guest OS to authenticate the guest operation as. Not this server's vCenter/ESXi credentials — a separate, guest-OS-local (or domain, if the guest is joined) account. |
| `is_volatile` | boolean | — | Create the key in memory only — it will NOT survive a guest reboot. Default false (persisted to disk). |
| `registry_path` | string | sim | Full path to the registry key, e.g. "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SOFTWARE\\MyApp". |

VMware Tools must be running in its guest OS (a Windows guest — these tools call the Windows-only GuestWindowsRegistryManager) for any of these tools to succeed. |
| `wow_bitness` | string | — | Which view of the Windows registry to access: "WOWNative" (default if omitted) — the native view (32-bit on a 32-bit guest, 64-bit on a 64-bit guest); "WOW32" — force the 32-bit view; "WOW64" — force the 64-bit view. See MSDN's WOW64 registry redirection docs. |

Requires VMware Tools running in the guest.

| `env_variables` | array&lt;string&gt; | — | Complete set of environment variables for the program, guest-OS notation (e.g. ["PATH=/usr/bin", "FOO=bar"]) — these REPLACE the default environment, they are not additions. Omit to use guest-dependent defaults. |
| `guest_password` | string | sim | Password for guest_username. |
| `guest_username` | string | sim | Username of a valid account inside the guest OS to authenticate the guest operation as. Not this server's vCenter/ESXi credentials — a separate, guest-OS-local (or domain, if the guest is joined) account. |
| `program_path` | string | sim | Absolute path, inside the guest, to the program to start. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. VMware Tools must be running in its guest OS for any guest-operations tool to succeed. |
| `working_directory` | string | — | Absolute path, inside the guest, of the working directory for the program. VMware recommends always setting this explicitly. Optional. |

### Health Update Manager (10)

#### `vmware_health_add_filter`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a HealthUpdateManager filter scoping which HealthUpdateInfo IDs from a provider are of interest. Reversible via vmware_health_remove_filter.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_health_add_filter(confirm, filter_name, provider_id, [info_ids])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `filter_name` | string | sim | Name for the new filter. |
| `info_ids` | array&lt;string&gt; | — | HealthUpdateInfo IDs to filter on. Omit/empty for no ID restriction. |
| `provider_id` | string | sim | The HealthUpdateProvider identifier (assigned by the extension/plugin that registers health monitoring for a component — e.g. a hardware health provider), as returned in the "providerId" of the entities/filters/updates it has registered. |

| `provider_id` | string | sim | The HealthUpdateProvider identifier (assigned by the extension/plugin that registers health monitoring for a component — e.g. a hardware health provider), as returned in the "providerId" of the entities/filters/updates it has registered. |

### Host - Account (3)

#### `vmware_host_account_create`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a local user account directly on an ESXi host. Works only when connected directly to an ESXi host (or, per vSphere's own API, hosts managed without a modern per-host account manager) — see this file's top doc comment for the ESXi-direct-only limitation confirmed against vcsim.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_account_create(confirm, host, user)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |
| `user` | object | sim | The account to create, matching types.HostAccountSpec: {"id": "...", "password": "...", "description": "..."}. "id" is required. |

#### `vmware_host_account_remove`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Remove a local user account directly from an ESXi host. Irreversible (the account and its settings are gone — re-creating an account with the same name is not the same account). Same ESXi-direct-only limitation as vmware_host_account_create (see this file's top doc comment).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_account_remove(confirm, host, user_name)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |
| `user_name` | string | sim | ID/name of the local account to remove. |

#### `vmware_host_account_update`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Update a local user account's password/description directly on an ESXi host. Same ESXi-direct-only limitation as vmware_host_account_create (see this file's top doc comment).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_account_update(confirm, host, user)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |
| `user` | object | sim | The account to update, matching types.HostAccountSpec: {"id": "...", "password": "...", "description": "..."}. "id" is required and identifies the existing account. |

### Host - Certificate (7)

#### `vmware_host_certificate_generate_csr`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Ask an ESXi host to generate a certificate-signing request (CSR) for itself, to be signed by a Certificate Authority and later imported via vmware_host_certificate_install_server_certificate. Kept at Tier 2 (not downgraded to read-only) — see this file's top doc comment for why a second call may invalidate a still-pending CSR's key on real vSphere even though vcsim's implementation is stateless.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_certificate_generate_csr(confirm, host, [use_ip_address_as_common_name])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |
| `use_ip_address_as_common_name` | boolean | — | Use the host's management IP address as the CSR's Common Name instead of its hostname. Default false. |

#### `vmware_host_certificate_generate_csr_by_dn`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Ask an ESXi host to generate a certificate-signing request (CSR) for itself using an explicit Distinguished Name, to be signed by a Certificate Authority and later imported via vmware_host_certificate_install_server_certificate. Kept at Tier 2 for the same reason as vmware_host_certificate_generate_csr (see this file's top doc comment) — not downgraded despite being structurally near-identical to that read-only-looking call.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_certificate_generate_csr_by_dn(confirm, distinguished_name, host)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `distinguished_name` | string | sim | The CSR's subject Distinguished Name, e.g. "CN=esxi-01.local,OU=IT,O=Example Corp,C=US". |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |

#### `vmware_host_certificate_info`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Get an ESXi host's current SSL certificate info (issuer, subject, validity, status, thumbprint).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_certificate_info(host)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |

#### `vmware_host_certificate_install_server_certificate`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Install (import) an SSL certificate as an ESXi host's active server certificate, typically one signed from a CSR obtained via vmware_host_certificate_generate_csr(_by_dn). Reversible only by installing another certificate — there is no "restore previous cert" tool. Some effects (per the real method's source) only fully apply after a service refresh the host performs internally.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_certificate_install_server_certificate(cert, confirm, host)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `cert` | string | sim | PEM-encoded X.509 certificate to install as the host's active server certificate. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |

#### `vmware_host_certificate_list_ca_certificates`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List the SSL certificates of Certificate Authorities trusted by an ESXi host.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_certificate_list_ca_certificates(host)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |

#### `vmware_host_certificate_list_ca_crls`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List the SSL certificate revocation lists (CRLs) of Certificate Authorities trusted by an ESXi host.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_certificate_list_ca_crls(host)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |

#### `vmware_host_certificate_replace_ca_certs_and_crls`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Replace the set of trusted Certificate Authority SSL certificates and/or CRLs an ESXi host uses to verify external entities. Reversible by calling this again with the previous lists. Omitting either list sends an empty list for that side (clears it), matching the real API's shape — pass both explicitly if you only intend to change one and keep the other.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_certificate_replace_ca_certs_and_crls(confirm, host, [ca_certificates, ca_crls])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `ca_certificates` | array&lt;string&gt; | — | PEM-encoded CA certificates to trust. Omit/empty clears the trusted CA certificate list. |
| `ca_crls` | array&lt;string&gt; | — | PEM-encoded CA certificate revocation lists to trust. Omit/empty clears the trusted CRL list. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |

| `spec` | object | sim | A types.VmfsDatastoreCreateSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields ("partition", "vmfs", "extent") — typically a VmfsDatastoreOption.spec value from vmware_host_datastore_query_vmfs_datastore_create_options. |

### Host - iSCSI (19)

#### `vmware_host_iscsi_add_send_targets`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Add SendTargets (dynamic discovery) addresses to an iSCSI HBA on a host. Reversible via vmware_host_iscsi_remove_send_targets.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_iscsi_add_send_targets(confirm, host, iscsi_hba_device, targets)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |

| `iscsi_hba_device` | string | sim | iSCSI HBA device name, e.g. "vmhba64" (the software iSCSI adapter) — see the host's storage adapters (HostHostBusAdapter.device). |

| `iscsi_hba_device` | string | sim | iSCSI HBA device name, e.g. "vmhba64" (the software iSCSI adapter) — see the host's storage adapters (HostHostBusAdapter.device). |

### Host - Maintenance (2)

#### `vmware_host_maintenance_enter`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Put an ESXi host into maintenance mode. On a standalone host (no cluster/DRS to evacuate powered-on VMs to) this can power off every VM running on it — treat it as destructive on that topology, not just a mode toggle.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_maintenance_enter(confirm, host, [evacuate, timeout])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `evacuate` | boolean | — | Evacuate powered-off VMs' storage to other hosts (only meaningful with DRS/a cluster — a no-op on standalone ESXi). Default false. |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |
| `timeout` | integer | — | Seconds to wait for the operation before giving up server-side. 0 (default) waits indefinitely. |

#### `vmware_host_maintenance_exit`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Take an ESXi host back out of maintenance mode.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_maintenance_exit(host, [timeout])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |
| `timeout` | integer | — | Seconds to wait for the operation before giving up server-side. 0 (default) waits indefinitely. |

#### `vmware_host_network_query_port_groups`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List the standard-switch port groups on an ESXi host with their current config (name, VLAN id, virtual switch, and the full HostPortGroupSpec incl. NIC teaming/security/traffic-shaping policy), plus the virtual switches. Read-only. Use this BEFORE vmware_host_network_update_port_group: that call REPLACES the entire port group spec, so take the returned "spec", change only the field(s) you want (e.g. vlanId), and send that complete spec back — a partial spec zeroes name/vswitchName/policy and breaks the port group.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_network_query_port_groups(host)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |

#### `vmware_host_network_update_network_config`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Apply a batch network configuration change to an ESXi host (virtual switches, port groups, physical/virtual NICs, DNS, IP routing). Complex and low-level — most callers want the narrower add_*/update_*/remove_* tools instead. See this file's top doc comment for how dns_config/ip_route_config/console_ip_route_config are handled separately from "config", and for the one unsupported field (NIC-teaming "bridge" spec on a vswitch/proxySwitch entry).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_network_update_network_config(change_mode, confirm, host, [config, console_ip_route_config, dns_config, ip_route_config])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `change_mode` | string | sim | "modify" merges config into the host's existing network config; "replace" overwrites it wholesale. |
| `config` | object | — | A types.HostNetworkConfig JSON object (vswitch, proxySwitch, portgroup, pnic, vnic, consoleVnic, routeTableConfig, dhcp, nat, ipV6Enabled, netStackSpec, migrationStatus fields). Do NOT nest dnsConfig/ipRouteConfig/consoleIpRouteConfig here — use the separate arguments below. Optional — omit for a zero-value config (only meaningful combined with the other arguments). |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `console_ip_route_config` | object | — | A types.HostIpRouteConfig JSON object for the service console's route. Optional. |
| `dns_config` | object | — | A types.HostDnsConfig JSON object — see vmware_host_network_update_dns_config's config for the shape. Optional. |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |
| `ip_route_config` | object | — | A types.HostIpRouteConfig JSON object. Optional. |

| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |
| `name` | string | — | Optional new name for the profile. |
| `profile` | string | sim | Host profile identifier: its exact "name" (as returned by vmware_host_profile_query_metadata or the "name" you gave vmware_host_profile_create), unique per connection. Profiles are not part of the inventory Folder tree — resolved by scanning HostProfileManager.profile[] and matching Profile.name exactly (case-sensitive, no glob support). |

### Host - Reboot (1)

#### `vmware_host_reboot`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Reboot an ESXi host, restarting its hypervisor. Every VM running on it goes down abruptly (no graceful guest shutdown) unless the guest OS reacts fast enough on its own — any unsaved state is lost. Tier 1: treated as high-risk/irreversible impact on running workloads, even though the host itself comes back up on its own.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_reboot(confirm, host, [force])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `force` | boolean | — | Force the operation even if the host is not in maintenance mode or has VMs running/other operations in progress. Optional, default false. |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |

|---|---|:--:|---|

### Host - Shutdown (1)

#### `vmware_host_shutdown`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Shut down an ESXi host, powering off its hypervisor entirely. Every VM running on it goes down abruptly. The host stays off until it is powered back on out-of-band (physical power button, IPMI/iLO/DRAC, Wake-on-LAN) — this server has no tool that can power it back on. Tier 1: same high-risk-impact reasoning as vmware_host_reboot, compounded by needing an out-of-band step to undo.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_shutdown(confirm, host, [force])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `force` | boolean | — | Force the operation even if the host is not in maintenance mode or has VMs running/other operations in progress. Optional, default false. |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |

### Host - vFlash (5)

#### `vmware_host_vflash_configure_cache`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Configure a host's vFlash swap cache: the default vFlash module for per-VM read/write caches and the amount of vFlash resource reserved for host swap cache. Setting the reservation to 0 disables the host swap cache. Reversible by calling again with different values.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_host_vflash_configure_cache(confirm, default_vflash_module, host, [swap_cache_reservation_gb])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `default_vflash_module` | string | sim | Name of the default vFlash module used for read-write caches associated with this host's VMs (can be overridden per-VMDK). |
| `host` | string | sim | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/esxi-01.local") as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |
| `swap_cache_reservation_gb` | integer | — | Amount of vFlash resource (in GB) reserved for the host swap cache. 0 (the default if omitted) disables the host swap cache. |

### IP Pool (8)

#### `vmware_ippool_allocate_ipv4`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Allocate an IPv4 address from a pool for allocation_id (idempotent — the same allocation_id returns the same address). Reversible via vmware_ippool_release_allocation.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_ippool_allocate_ipv4(allocation_id, confirm, dc, pool_id)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `allocation_id` | string | sim | Caller-chosen unique identifier for this allocation (e.g. a VM's instance UUID or MoRef value). Allocating twice with the same allocation_id against the same pool returns the same IP rather than allocating a second one. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `dc` | string | sim | Datacenter identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. IP pools are scoped to a datacenter. |
| `pool_id` | integer | sim | The pool's unique numeric ID, as returned by vmware_ippool_create's "pool_id" field or vmware_ippool_query's per-entry "id" field. |

#### `vmware_ippool_allocate_ipv6`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Allocate an IPv6 address from a pool for allocation_id (idempotent — the same allocation_id returns the same address). Reversible via vmware_ippool_release_allocation.

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `allocation_id` | string | sim | Caller-chosen unique identifier for this allocation (e.g. a VM's instance UUID or MoRef value). Allocating twice with the same allocation_id against the same pool returns the same IP rather than allocating a second one. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `dc` | string | sim | Datacenter identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. IP pools are scoped to a datacenter. |
| `pool_id` | integer | sim | The pool's unique numeric ID, as returned by vmware_ippool_create's "pool_id" field or vmware_ippool_query's per-entry "id" field. |

#### `vmware_ippool_create`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new IP pool on a datacenter. Reversible via vmware_ippool_destroy.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_ippool_create(confirm, dc, pool)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `dc` | string | sim | Datacenter identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. IP pools are scoped to a datacenter. |
| `pool` | object | sim | IpPool spec. "name" required on create. "id" is required on update (identifies the pool to update) and ignored on create (the server assigns it). At least one of ipv4Config/ipv6Config should be set for the pool to be usable. |

#### `vmware_ippool_destroy`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Permanently delete an IP pool. Irreversible — the pool definition is gone; re-creating it requires vmware_ippool_create with the same spec.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_ippool_destroy(confirm, dc, pool_id, [force])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `dc` | string | sim | Datacenter identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. IP pools are scoped to a datacenter. |
| `force` | boolean | — | Destroy even if the pool has active allocations. Defaults to false. |
| `pool_id` | integer | sim | The pool's unique numeric ID, as returned by vmware_ippool_create's "pool_id" field or vmware_ippool_query's per-entry "id" field. |

List the IP pools defined on a datacenter.

|---|---|:--:|---|
| `dc` | string | sim | Datacenter identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. IP pools are scoped to a datacenter. |

Look up the IP address (IPv4 and/or IPv6) currently allocated under a given extension_key on a pool.

### Content Library (68)

#### `vmware_library_add_library_item_file`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Add a file to an update session (POST .../updatesession/file/{session_id}?~action=add). file_spec matches library.UpdateFile's JSON shape: {"name": "...", "source_type": "PUSH"|"PULL", "source_endpoint": {"uri": "...", "ssl_certificate": "...", "ssl_certificate_thumbprint": "..."} (required when source_type is PULL), "checksum_info": {"algorithm": "...", "checksum": "..."}}. For PUSH, the response's upload_endpoint.uri is where the caller must separately PUT the file bytes — this server has no byte-transfer tool. For a simpler PULL-from-URL flow, prefer vmware_library_add_library_item_file_from_uri instead.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_library_add_library_item_file(confirm, file_spec, session_id)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `file_spec` | object | sim | A library.UpdateFile JSON object — see this tool's description for the shape. |
| `session_id` | string | sim | Update session ID, as returned by vmware_library_create_library_item_update_session. |

#### `vmware_library_add_library_item_file_from_uri`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Add a file to an update session by pulling it from a remote http(s) URI (AddLibraryItemFileFromURI — probes the URI first via HEAD/ProbeTransferEndpoint, then adds it as a PULL-source file). "checksum" is optional: 0 or 1 objects of {"algorithm": "...", "checksum": "..."} — passing 2+ fails with the real API's own "expected 0 or 1 checksum" error.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_library_add_library_item_file_from_uri(confirm, name, session_id, uri, [checksum])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `checksum` | array&lt;object&gt; | — | 0 or 1 checksum objects: [{"algorithm": "SHA1"\|"SHA256"\|..., "checksum": "hex digest"}]. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `name` | string | sim | Destination file name within the library item. |
| `session_id` | string | sim | Update session ID, as returned by vmware_library_create_library_item_update_session. |
| `uri` | string | sim | Source http(s) URL to pull the file from. |

#### `vmware_library_copy_item`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Copy a library item to a new item (same or different library). Returns the new item's ID.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_library_copy_item(confirm, destination, source_item_id)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `destination` | object | sim | A library.Item JSON object describing the destination item, e.g. {"name": "...", "library_id": "...", "description": "..."}. Passed through as the copy's destination_create_spec. |
| `source_item_id` | string | sim | Library item ID (a server-generated opaque string) as returned by vmware_library_create_item, vmware_library_list_items, or vmware_library_find_items. Not an item name. |

#### `vmware_library_create_item`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new (empty) item in a content library. Returns the new item's ID. Content is added separately (out of this group's scope — no upload-session tools are registered here).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_library_create_item(confirm, item)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `item` | object | sim | A library.Item JSON object. Required: "name", "library_id" (the destination library — see vmware_library_list_libraries), "type" (e.g. "iso", "ovf", "vm-template"). Optional: "description". Every other field is ignored even if supplied — the server only forwards these 4. |

#### `vmware_library_create_library`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new content library (LOCAL, backed by a datastore, or SUBSCRIBED, pulling from another library's publish URL). Returns the new library's ID.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_library_create_library(confirm, library)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `library` | object | sim | A library.Library JSON object (matching its Go struct's json tags — referencia/govmomi/vapi/library/library.go). Required: "name", "type" ("LOCAL" or "SUBSCRIBED"), and "storage_backings" (an array of {"datastore_id": "<datastore moref value, e.g. from vmware_list_datastores>", "type": "DATASTORE"}) — storage_backings is required for BOTH types against this server, not just LOCAL as the Go source's doc comment alone would suggest (empirically confirmed: vcsim's own library-creation handler indexes storage_backings[0] unconditionally to compute the new library's on-disk path and panics on an empty array — see this file's top doc comment). For type="SUBSCRIBED", additionally required: "subscription_info", an object {"subscription_url": "<https URL to another library's publish_url>", "authentication_method": "NONE"\|"BASIC", "user_name", "password", "ssl_thumbprint" (optional — auto-fetched via TLS if subscription_url is https and this is omitted), "automatic_sync_enabled", "on_demand"}. Optional either way: "description", "publish_info" (object: "authentication_method", "published" bool, "user_name", "password"), "security_policy_id", "configuration_info" (object: {"apply_library_usage_to_items": bool}). Server-generated fields ("id", "creation_time", "last_modified_time", "last_sync_time", "server_guid", "state_info") are ignored if supplied. |

#### `vmware_library_create_subscriber`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a subscription of a published library, associating an already-existing SUBSCRIBED library on this server as the subscriber. Returns the new subscription's ID.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_library_create_subscriber(confirm, library_id, subscriber)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `library_id` | string | sim | Content library ID (a server-generated opaque string, e.g. "d0055587-9d01-4b31-9e35-1a2b3c4d5e6f") as returned by vmware_library_create_library, vmware_library_list_libraries, vmware_library_find_library, or vmware_library_get_library_by_name. Not a library name. |
| `subscriber` | object | sim | A library.SubscriberLibrary JSON object. Required: "target" (a free-form location/hostname label recorded on the subscription), "location" (free-form), "subscribed_library" (the ID of an ALREADY-EXISTING library on this server that represents the subscriber side — typically one created earlier with vmware_library_create_library type="SUBSCRIBED" — see this file's top doc comment for why this is empirically required, not just documented). Optional: "vcenter" (object: "hostname", "https_port", "server_guid"), "placement" (object: "resource_pool", "host", "folder", "cluster", "network"). |

#### `vmware_library_find_items`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Find library item IDs matching any combination of library, name, type, source item ID, and cached state. Omit every field to list every item in the system, same as calling vmware_library_get_libraries + vmware_library_list_items per library.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_library_find_items([cached, library_id, name, source_id, type])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `cached` | boolean | — | Match only items whose cached content matches this value. Omit to match either. |
| `library_id` | string | — | Restrict the search to this library ID. Omit to search every library. |
| `name` | string | — | Item name to match. Omit to match every name. |
| `source_id` | string | — | For items in a SUBSCRIBED library, the source item ID on the published library. Omit to match any. |
| `type` | string | — | Item type to match, e.g. "iso", "ovf", "vm-template". Omit to match every type. |

#### `vmware_library_find_library`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Find content library IDs matching a name (case-insensitive) and/or type. Omit both to list every library, same as vmware_library_list_libraries.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_library_find_library([name, type])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `name` | string | — | Case-insensitive library name to match. Omit to match every name. |
| `type` | string | — | Library type to match: "LOCAL" or "SUBSCRIBED". Omit to match either. |

#### `vmware_library_finder_find`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Find content library objects (libraries, items, or files) by inventory path(s) of the form "LIBRARY/ITEM/FILE" — e.g. "my-library" (list matching libraries), "my-library/my-item" (list matching items), or "my-library/*.ova" (wildcard-match items/files). Both "*" and "?" glob wildcards are supported; a path segment with no wildcard is resolved via a direct server-side lookup instead of a full listing. Omit "paths" (or pass an empty list) to list every library.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_library_finder_find([paths])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `paths` | array&lt;string&gt; | — | One or more inventory path patterns to search for, e.g. ["my-library/*.ova", "other-library/template-a"]. Defaults to matching every library if omitted. |

| `uri` | string | sim | http(s) URL to probe. |

#### `vmware_library_wait_on_library_item_update_session`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`

Block until an update session leaves the ACTIVE state (e.g. after vmware_library_complete_library_item_update_session), then return its final state. Fuses object-model WaitOnLibraryItemUpdateSession's client-side progress callback out (no JSON-RPC representation — see this file's top doc comment) and always bounds the wait with timeout_seconds (default 300s) so a stuck/orphaned session cannot block the server indefinitely. Returns an error if the session ends in the ERROR state.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_library_wait_on_library_item_update_session(session_id, [poll_interval_seconds, timeout_seconds])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `poll_interval_seconds` | integer | — | Delay between polls, in seconds. Default 2. |
| `session_id` | string | sim | Update session ID, as returned by vmware_library_create_library_item_update_session. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | — | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever. Default 300 (5 minutes) if omitted. |

### Licencas (13)

#### `vmware_license_add`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Add a license key to this connection's list of available licenses. If the key is already present, returns its existing info without duplicating it.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_license_add(confirm, license_key, [labels])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `labels` | array&lt;object&gt; | — | Optional key-value labels to attach to the license (types.KeyValue[]). Per the API's own doc comment, ignored by ESX Server — meaningful against vCenter. |
| `license_key` | string | sim | A license key, e.g. a serial number ("XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX"), as returned by vmware_license_decode/vmware_license_add or listed under "licenses" in this connection's LicenseManager. |

#### `vmware_license_check_feature`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Check whether a specific license feature is currently enabled/available on this connection (or, if host is given, a specific host).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_license_check_feature(feature_key, [host])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `feature_key` | string | sim | Name of the feature to check, e.g. "dvs" or "vmotion" — see vmware_license_query_supported_features for the list of keys this connection recognizes. |
| `host` | string | — | Optional host identifier (name/pattern, e.g. "esxi-01.local", or a full inventory path) as returned by vmware_list_hosts — "host to act on if LicenseManager is not on a host" per the real API's own doc comment. Meaningful against a vCenter's LicenseManager (which is not bound to any single host); omit when connected directly to a standalone ESXi host, whose LicenseManager already applies to that host. |

#### `vmware_license_configure_source`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Reconfigure this connection's (or, if host is given, a specific host's) license source — switch between a local license key, a license server, or evaluation mode. Reversible by calling again with a different source.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_license_configure_source(confirm, license_source, [host])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host` | string | — | Optional host identifier (name/pattern, e.g. "esxi-01.local", or a full inventory path) as returned by vmware_list_hosts — "host to act on if LicenseManager is not on a host" per the real API's own doc comment. Meaningful against a vCenter's LicenseManager (which is not bound to any single host); omit when connected directly to a standalone ESXi host, whose LicenseManager already applies to that host. |
| `license_source` | object | sim | The license source to configure, one of 3 shapes selected by "type": {"type":"local","license_keys":"..."} (types.LocalLicenseSource — a locally-installed license key string), {"type":"served","license_server":"host:port"} (types.LicenseServerSource — a license server to connect to), or {"type":"evaluation"} (types.EvaluationLicenseSource — revert to evaluation mode). |

#### `vmware_license_set_edition`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Select this connection's (or, if host is given, a specific host's) license edition by feature key. Passing an empty feature_key makes the product unlicensed (per the API's own doc comment) — reversible by calling again with a valid feature_key.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_license_set_edition(confirm, [feature_key, host])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `feature_key` | string | — | Name of the edition feature to select, e.g. "vc.standard". Empty/omitted makes the product unlicensed. |
| `host` | string | — | Optional host identifier (name/pattern, e.g. "esxi-01.local", or a full inventory path) as returned by vmware_list_hosts — "host to act on if LicenseManager is not on a host" per the real API's own doc comment. Meaningful against a vCenter's LicenseManager (which is not bound to any single host); omit when connected directly to a standalone ESXi host, whose LicenseManager already applies to that host. |

#### `vmware_license_update`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Update an already-added license key's labels (replaces any existing labels for that key). Fails if the key was never added via vmware_license_add.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_license_update(confirm, license_key, [labels])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `labels` | array&lt;object&gt; | — | Optional key-value labels to attach to the license (types.KeyValue[]). Per the API's own doc comment, ignored by ESX Server — meaningful against vCenter. |
| `license_key` | string | sim | A license key, e.g. a serial number ("XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX"), as returned by vmware_license_decode/vmware_license_add or listed under "licenses" in this connection's LicenseManager. |

#### `vmware_license_update_assigned`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Assign a license key to an entity (vCenter only — see this file's top doc comment), e.g. a host. Reversible via vmware_license_update_assigned (re-assign a different key) or vmware_license_remove_assigned.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_license_update_assigned(confirm, entity_id, license_key, [entity_display_name])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `entity_display_name` | string | — | Optional display name for the entity, shown in the assignment listing. |
| `entity_id` | string | sim | ID of the entity a license is assigned to (e.g. a HostSystem). Read this from a prior vmware_license_query_assigned call's own "entity_id" output rather than constructing it — the exact ID scheme (host hardware UUID vs. something else) is server-dependent. |
| `license_key` | string | sim | A license key, e.g. a serial number ("XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX"), as returned by vmware_license_decode/vmware_license_add or listed under "licenses" in this connection's LicenseManager. |

#### `vmware_license_update_label`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Set (or, if label_value is an empty string, remove) a single key-value label on an already-added license key. Ignored by ESX Server per the API's own doc comment — meaningful against vCenter.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_license_update_label(confirm, label_key, label_value, license_key)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `label_key` | string | sim | The label's key. |
| `label_value` | string | sim | The label's new value. An empty string removes the label if it already exists (or creates an empty-value label if it doesn't). |
| `license_key` | string | sim | A license key, e.g. a serial number ("XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX"), as returned by vmware_license_decode/vmware_license_add or listed under "licenses" in this connection's LicenseManager. |

### Inventario - Listagens (7)

#### `vmware_list_clusters`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List clusters (ClusterComputeResource) visible to the connected session. Empty on a standalone ESXi host or a vCenter with no clusters configured — that is expected, not an error.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_list_clusters([path])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `path` | string | — | Name pattern (govmomi find syntax) matched under every datacenter's host folder, e.g. "*" for all or "cluster-*" to filter by name. Pass a full inventory path starting with "/" to scope to one datacenter instead. Defaults to "*". |

#### `vmware_list_datacenters`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List datacenters visible to the connected session. A standalone ESXi host always reports exactly one ("ha-datacenter").

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_list_datacenters([path])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `path` | string | — | Name pattern (govmomi find syntax), e.g. "*" for all. Defaults to "*". |

#### `vmware_list_datastores`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List datastores visible to the connected session, with capacity/free space/accessibility summary.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_list_datastores([path])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `path` | string | — | Name pattern (govmomi find syntax) matched under every datacenter's datastore folder, e.g. "*" for all or "datastore1" to filter by name. Pass a full inventory path starting with "/" to scope to one datacenter instead. Defaults to "*". |

#### `vmware_list_hosts`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List ESXi hosts visible to the connected session under an inventory path pattern.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_list_hosts([path])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `path` | string | — | Name pattern (govmomi find syntax) matched under every datacenter's host folder, e.g. "*" for all or "esxi-*" to filter by name. Pass a full inventory path starting with "/" to scope to one datacenter instead. Defaults to "*". |

#### `vmware_list_networks`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List networks (standard port groups, opaque networks, and distributed port groups) visible to the connected session.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_list_networks([path])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `path` | string | — | Name pattern (govmomi find syntax) matched under every datacenter's network folder, e.g. "*" for all or "VM Network" to filter by name. Pass a full inventory path starting with "/" to scope to one datacenter instead. Defaults to "*". |

#### `vmware_list_resource_pools`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List resource pools visible to the connected session (every ComputeResource/ClusterComputeResource has at least an implicit "Resources" pool).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_list_resource_pools([path])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|

#### `vmware_list_vms`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List virtual machines visible to the connected session under an inventory path pattern (govmomi find syntax).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_list_vms([path])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `path` | string | — | Name pattern (govmomi find syntax) matched under every datacenter's VM folder, e.g. "*" for all VMs or "web*" to filter by name. Pass a full inventory path starting with "/" (e.g. "/MyDatacenter/vm/*") to scope to one datacenter instead. Defaults to "*". |

| `load_balancer_config_spec` | object | — | {"id": "...", "provider": "HA_PROXY\|AVI", "address_ranges": [...], "ha_proxy_config_create_spec": {...}, "avi_config_create_spec": {...}}. |

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Update (replace) a Virtual Machine Class's CPU/memory/device profile. Behaves as a full replace, not a partial patch — every field is re-sent; fields omitted here fall back to their zero value except id, which defaults to vm_class if omitted.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_namespace_update_vm_class(confirm, cpu_count, memory_mb, vm_class, [config_spec, cpu_reservation, devices, id, memory_reservation])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `config_spec` | object | — | Optional raw/version-specific extended VM Class config spec, passed through verbatim. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `cpu_count` | integer | sim | Number of virtual CPUs. |
| `cpu_reservation` | integer | — | CPU reservation percentage (0-100). Optional. |
| `devices` | object | — | Optional passthrough devices: {"direct_path_io_devices": [...], "vgpu_devices": [...]}. |
| `id` | string | — | VM Class ID for the updated spec's body. Defaults to vm_class if omitted — only override this if you specifically need to test/observe a mismatch. |
| `memory_mb` | integer | sim | Memory in MB. |
| `memory_reservation` | integer | — | Memory reservation percentage (0-100). Optional. |
| `vm_class` | string | sim | Virtual Machine Class ID (e.g. "best-effort-2xlarge", or a custom class ID created via vmware_namespace_create_vm_class). |

### Performance (metricas) (9)

#### `vmware_perf_interval_create`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new custom historical statistics interval (sampling period, retention length, name). Reversible via vmware_perf_interval_remove (which discards any statistics collected under it).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_perf_interval_create(confirm, interval)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `interval` | object | sim | A PerfInterval. Properties: "key" (integer, unique interval ID), "name" (string), "samplingPeriod" (integer, seconds of data granularity), "length" (integer, seconds statistics are retained), "level" (integer 1-4), "enabled" (boolean). |

#### `vmware_perf_interval_remove`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Remove a historical statistics interval by its sampling period. Irreversible: any statistics VirtualCenter already retained under that interval are discarded and cannot be recovered by recreating the interval.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_perf_interval_remove(confirm, sample_period)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `sample_period` | integer | sim | The samplingPeriod (in seconds) of the historical interval to remove. |

#### `vmware_perf_interval_update`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Update an existing historical statistics interval's name, sampling period, retention length, level, or enabled state. Reversible via another update.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_perf_interval_update(confirm, interval)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `interval` | object | sim | A PerfInterval. Properties: "key" (integer, unique interval ID), "name" (string), "samplingPeriod" (integer, seconds of data granularity), "length" (integer, seconds statistics are retained), "level" (integer 1-4), "enabled" (boolean). |

#### `vmware_perf_provider_summary`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Get performance-provider summary info for a managed entity: whether current (real-time) and/or summary (historical) stats are supported, and the real-time refresh rate.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_perf_provider_summary(entity_path)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `entity_path` | string | sim | Full inventory path of the managed entity to query (e.g. "/DC0/vm/my-vm", "/DC0/host/cluster1/esxi-01.local"), resolved via SearchIndex.FindByInventoryPath. Works for any performance-provider entity kind: VirtualMachine, HostSystem, ResourcePool, ClusterComputeResource, Datastore, Datacenter. |

#### `vmware_perf_query`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Retrieve performance statistics for one or more managed entities (VMs, hosts, clusters, resource pools, datastores, datacenters) matching one or more PerfQuerySpec queries. The core vSphere performance-metrics query operation.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_perf_query(query_specs)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `query_specs` | array&lt;object&gt; | sim | One or more query specs (see items schema). Each entry can query a different entity and/or different metrics. |

#### `vmware_perf_query_available_metric`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List the performance metrics (counterId + instance pairs) actually available for a managed entity over an optional time range/interval — narrower and entity-specific, unlike vmware_perf_query_counter/vmware_perf_query_counter_by_level which list every counter the system knows about.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_perf_query_available_metric(entity_path, [begin_time, end_time, interval_id])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `begin_time` | string | — | Optional RFC3339 timestamp. Defaults to the oldest available metric for the entity. |
| `end_time` | string | — | Optional RFC3339 timestamp. Defaults to the most recently generated metric for the entity. |
| `entity_path` | string | sim | Full inventory path of the managed entity to query (e.g. "/DC0/vm/my-vm", "/DC0/host/cluster1/esxi-01.local"), resolved via SearchIndex.FindByInventoryPath. Works for any performance-provider entity kind: VirtualMachine, HostSystem, ResourcePool, ClusterComputeResource, Datastore, Datacenter. |
| `interval_id` | integer | — | Optional interval (a real-time provider's refreshRate or a historical interval's samplingPeriod). Defaults to available metrics for historical statistics. |

#### `vmware_perf_query_composite`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Retrieve aggregated (rolled up) performance statistics for a managed entity and its children in one call — e.g. a cluster's aggregate CPU usage across its hosts. Requires metricId in the query spec.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_perf_query_composite(query_spec)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `query_spec` | object | sim | A PerfQuerySpec. Properties: "entity_path" (string, required — see this tool's entity_path argument for the format), "startTime"/"endTime" (optional RFC3339 timestamp strings — server time range to retrieve; omit both for the most recent sample(s)), "maxSample" (optional integer — limits the number of samples returned, only meaningful with intervalId set to a real-time refreshRate), "metricId" (optional array of {"counterId": <int, from vmware_perf_query_counter/vmware_perf_query_counter_by_level>, "instance": <string, "" for aggregate, "*" for every instance>} — omit for every available metric), "intervalId" (optional integer — a real-time provider's refreshRate for current stats, or a historical interval's samplingPeriod for historical stats; see vmware_perf_provider_summary and vmware_perf_interval list of historical intervals), "format" (optional "normal" or "csv", defaults to "normal"). |

#### `vmware_perf_query_counter`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Look up performance counter metadata (name, group, unit, rollup type, stats type, level) for one or more counter IDs.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_perf_query_counter(counter_ids)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `counter_ids` | array&lt;integer&gt; | sim | One or more performance counter IDs, e.g. as returned in metricId.counterId by vmware_perf_query_available_metric. |

#### `vmware_perf_query_counter_by_level`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

List every performance counter available at or below a given statistics collection level (1-4).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_perf_query_counter_by_level(level)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `level` | integer | sim | Collection level, 1 through 4 (higher levels include more counters). |

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `name` | string | sim | Name for the new child resource pool. |
| `resource_pool` | string | sim | Resource pool identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "Resources") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/Resources") as returned by vmware_list_resource_pools. Must resolve to exactly one resource pool. |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.ResourceConfigSpec JSON object matching its Go struct field names. Real vSphere/vcsim requires "cpuAllocation" and "memoryAllocation" to be FULLY specified — all 4 sub-fields ("reservation", "limit", "expandableReservation", "shares") on each — a partially-specified allocation is rejected with InvalidArgument. Example: {"cpuAllocation":{"reservation":0,"limit":-1,"expandableReservation":true,"shares":{"level":"normal","shares":4000}},"memoryAllocation":{"reservation":0,"limit":-1,"expandableReservation":true,"shares":{"level":"normal","shares":163840}}}. |

#### `vmware_resource_pool_create_vapp`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new vApp under an existing resource pool. NOTE: vApp creation is a real vCenter-only vSphere capability (esx.ResourcePool.DisabledMethod disables this on standalone ESXi — see this file's top doc comment) — this call fails cleanly (not a crash) against a standalone-ESXi connection.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_resource_pool_create_vapp(confirm, name, res_spec, resource_pool, [config_spec, folder])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `config_spec` | object | — | Optional types.VAppConfigSpec JSON object matching its Go struct field names (e.g. "annotation", "product"). Omit for a bare vApp with no OVF product metadata. |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `folder` | string | — | Destination inventory folder for the vApp: a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm") or a subfolder name/pattern under the datacenter's "vm" folder, resolved the same way vmware_vm_clone's "folder" argument is. Omit to use the datacenter's root VM folder. |
| `name` | string | sim | Name for the new vApp. |
| `res_spec` | object | sim | A types.ResourceConfigSpec JSON object matching its Go struct field names. Real vSphere/vcsim requires "cpuAllocation" and "memoryAllocation" to be FULLY specified — all 4 sub-fields ("reservation", "limit", "expandableReservation", "shares") on each — a partially-specified allocation is rejected with InvalidArgument. Example: {"cpuAllocation":{"reservation":0,"limit":-1,"expandableReservation":true,"shares":{"level":"normal","shares":4000}},"memoryAllocation":{"reservation":0,"limit":-1,"expandableReservation":true,"shares":{"level":"normal","shares":163840}}}. |
| `resource_pool` | string | sim | Resource pool identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "Resources") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/Resources") as returned by vmware_list_resource_pools. Must resolve to exactly one resource pool. |

#### `vmware_resource_pool_import_vapp`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Start an OVF/OVA import lease for a single virtual machine under a resource pool and return the uploadable device (VMDK/OVF) URLs once the lease is ready. Does not upload the files itself — a caller uploads to the returned URLs separately, then marks the lease complete out of band. Only single-VM imports (types.VirtualMachineImportSpec) are supported — a multi-VM vApp tree import (types.VirtualAppImportSpec) is out of scope for this MVP (see this file's top doc comment).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_resource_pool_import_vapp(confirm, resource_pool, spec, [folder, host])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `folder` | string | — | Destination inventory folder for the imported VM, resolved the same way vmware_vm_clone's "folder" argument is. Omit to use the datacenter's root VM folder. |
| `host` | string | — | Target ESXi host identifier (see vmware_list_hosts). Optional — omit to let vSphere pick. |
| `resource_pool` | string | sim | Resource pool identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "Resources") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/Resources") as returned by vmware_list_resource_pools. Must resolve to exactly one resource pool. |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.VirtualMachineImportSpec JSON object matching its Go struct field names — "configSpec" (a types.VirtualMachineConfigSpec; at minimum "name" and "files":{"vmPathName":"[datastore1] my-vm"}) is the practically-required part, "resPoolEntity" is optional/deprecated. See referencia/govmomi/vim25/types/types.go's VirtualMachineImportSpec/VirtualMachineConfigSpec for the full field list. |

| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
