### Scheduled Tasks (7)

#### `vmware_scheduledtask_create`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new scheduled task on a managed entity (VM, host, cluster, datacenter, folder, or resource pool — the action applies to every VM/host descendant if the entity isn't a leaf). Reversible via vmware_scheduledtask_remove.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_scheduledtask_create(confirm, spec, [entity, host, vm])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `entity` | object | — | Explicit MoRef of the target managed object/entity, e.g. {"type": "ClusterComputeResource", "value": "domain-c7"} — use this to target a kind vmware_list_vms/vmware_list_hosts can't resolve directly. Alternative to "vm"/"host". |
| `host` | string | — | Host identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Alternative to "entity"/"vm". |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.ScheduledTaskSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields — "name" (string, required), "enabled" (bool, required), "scheduler" (object, required, see below), "action" (object, required, see below), "description" (string), "notification" (string, email address for completion notification, empty = none).  "scheduler" is vSphere's polymorphic (xsi:type) TaskScheduler field — encode the concrete type as a JSON object carrying a "_vimType" discriminator naming the exact govmomi struct. All variants also accept optional "activeTime"/"expireTime" (RFC3339 timestamps; activeTime defaults to creation time, expireTime defaults to never).   scheduler._vimType one of:     "OnceTaskScheduler"             {"runAt": "RFC3339 timestamp, optional — omit to run immediately once activated"}     "AfterStartupTaskScheduler"     {"minute": int32 — delay in minutes after vCenter Server restarts}     "HourlyTaskScheduler"           {"interval": int32 (1-999, default 1), "minute": int32 (0-59, UTC)}     "DailyTaskScheduler"            {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32 (0-23, UTC)}     "WeeklyTaskScheduler"           {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32, "sunday".."saturday": bool (at least one must be true)}     "MonthlyByDayTaskScheduler"     {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32, "day": int32 (1-31)}     "MonthlyByWeekdayTaskScheduler" {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32, "offset": "first"\|"second"\|"third"\|"fourth"\|"last", "weekday": "sunday".."saturday"}  "action" is the same BaseAction leaf shape vmware_alarm_create's spec.action.action uses (_vimType one of "SendEmailAction"\|"SendSNMPAction"\|"RunScriptAction"\|"CreateTaskAction"\|"MethodAction") — see vmware_alarm_create's description for each leaf's fields. |
| `vm` | string | — | VM identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_vms. Alternative to "entity"/"host". |

#### `vmware_scheduledtask_create_object`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new scheduled task on any managed object (broader than vmware_scheduledtask_create's ManagedEntity restriction — e.g. a HostVStorageObjectManager or other non-entity managed object may also be a valid target for some actions). Reversible via vmware_scheduledtask_remove.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_scheduledtask_create_object(confirm, spec, [entity, host, vm])`

| `entity` | object | — | Explicit MoRef of the target managed object/entity, e.g. {"type": "ClusterComputeResource", "value": "domain-c7"} — use this to target a kind vmware_list_vms/vmware_list_hosts can't resolve directly. Alternative to "vm"/"host". Despite the argument name, this may be ANY managed object, not only an entity. |
| `host` | string | — | Host identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Alternative to "entity"/"vm". |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.ScheduledTaskSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields — "name" (string, required), "enabled" (bool, required), "scheduler" (object, required, see below), "action" (object, required, see below), "description" (string), "notification" (string, email address for completion notification, empty = none).  "scheduler" is vSphere's polymorphic (xsi:type) TaskScheduler field — encode the concrete type as a JSON object carrying a "_vimType" discriminator naming the exact govmomi struct. All variants also accept optional "activeTime"/"expireTime" (RFC3339 timestamps; activeTime defaults to creation time, expireTime defaults to never).   scheduler._vimType one of:     "OnceTaskScheduler"             {"runAt": "RFC3339 timestamp, optional — omit to run immediately once activated"}     "AfterStartupTaskScheduler"     {"minute": int32 — delay in minutes after vCenter Server restarts}     "HourlyTaskScheduler"           {"interval": int32 (1-999, default 1), "minute": int32 (0-59, UTC)}     "DailyTaskScheduler"            {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32 (0-23, UTC)}     "WeeklyTaskScheduler"           {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32, "sunday".."saturday": bool (at least one must be true)}     "MonthlyByDayTaskScheduler"     {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32, "day": int32 (1-31)}     "MonthlyByWeekdayTaskScheduler" {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32, "offset": "first"\|"second"\|"third"\|"fourth"\|"last", "weekday": "sunday".."saturday"}  "action" is the same BaseAction leaf shape vmware_alarm_create's spec.action.action uses (_vimType one of "SendEmailAction"\|"SendSNMPAction"\|"RunScriptAction"\|"CreateTaskAction"\|"MethodAction") — see vmware_alarm_create's description for each leaf's fields. |
| `vm` | string | — | VM identifier: a name/pattern or inventory path, as returned by vmware_list_vms. Alternative to "entity"/"host". |

"scheduler" is vSphere's polymorphic (xsi:type) TaskScheduler field — encode the concrete type as a JSON object carrying a "_vimType" discriminator naming the exact govmomi struct. All variants also accept optional "activeTime"/"expireTime" (RFC3339 timestamps; activeTime defaults to creation time, expireTime defaults to never).   scheduler._vimType one of:     "OnceTaskScheduler"             {"runAt": "RFC3339 timestamp, optional — omit to run immediately once activated"}     "AfterStartupTaskScheduler"     {"minute": int32 — delay in minutes after vCenter Server restarts}     "HourlyTaskScheduler"           {"interval": int32 (1-999, default 1), "minute": int32 (0-59, UTC)}     "DailyTaskScheduler"            {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32 (0-23, UTC)}     "WeeklyTaskScheduler"           {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32, "sunday".."saturday": bool (at least one must be true)}     "MonthlyByDayTaskScheduler"     {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32, "day": int32 (1-31)}     "MonthlyByWeekdayTaskScheduler" {"interval": int32, "minute": int32, "hour": int32, "offset": "first"\|"second"\|"third"\|"fourth"\|"last", "weekday": "sunday".."saturday"}  "action" is the same BaseAction leaf shape vmware_alarm_create's spec.action.action uses (_vimType one of "SendEmailAction"\|"SendSNMPAction"\|"RunScriptAction"\|"CreateTaskAction"\|"MethodAction") — see vmware_alarm_create's description for each leaf's fields. |

### Storage DRS / SDRS (9)

#### `vmware_storage_apply_drs_recommendation`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Apply one or more previously computed Storage DRS recommendations (see vmware_storage_recommend_datastores) by key, triggering the underlying disk/VM relocation(s).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_storage_apply_drs_recommendation(confirm, key)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |

| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `key` | array&lt;string&gt; | sim | Recommendation key(s) (ClusterRecommendation.key) to act on — typically obtained from a prior vmware_storage_recommend_datastores call's result. |

#### `vmware_storage_apply_drs_recommendation_to_pod`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Apply a single previously computed Storage DRS recommendation by key, scoped to a specific datastore cluster (StoragePod).

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `key` | string | sim | Recommendation key (ClusterRecommendation.key) to apply. |
| `pod` | string | sim | Datastore cluster (StoragePod) name/pattern (e.g. "pod1") or a full inventory path. Must resolve to exactly one datastore cluster. |

#### `vmware_storage_cancel_drs_recommendation`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Discard one or more pending Storage DRS recommendations by key without applying them — they will not be re-offered and must be recomputed via vmware_storage_recommend_datastores/vmware_storage_refresh_drs_recommendation if still needed.

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `key` | array&lt;string&gt; | sim | Recommendation key(s) (ClusterRecommendation.key) to act on — typically obtained from a prior vmware_storage_recommend_datastores call's result. |

#### `vmware_storage_configure_datastore_iorm`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Configure Storage I/O Resource Management (IORM/Storage I/O Control) settings for a datastore. The "key" argument is accepted for Go-signature fidelity but is NOT sent to the server by govmomi's own client wrapper — confirmed by reading the real method body; it has no effect and exists only if a future govmomi version starts using it.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_storage_configure_datastore_iorm(confirm, datastore, spec, [key])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `datastore` | string | sim | Datastore name/pattern (e.g. "datastore1") as returned by vmware_list_datastores. Must resolve to exactly one datastore. |
| `key` | string | — | Accepted but currently ignored — see this tool's description. |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.StorageIORMConfigSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields (e.g. {"enabled": true, "congestionThreshold": 30}). |

#### `vmware_storage_configure_drs_for_pod`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Configure Storage DRS settings (enable/disable, default VM behavior, load-balance interval, per-VM overrides) for a datastore cluster (StoragePod).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_storage_configure_drs_for_pod(confirm, pod, spec, [modify])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `modify` | boolean | — | If true (default false/zero value), spec is applied incrementally on top of the existing configuration; if false, the pod's configuration is replaced to match spec exactly. |
| `pod` | string | sim | Datastore cluster (StoragePod) name/pattern (e.g. "pod1") or a full inventory path. Must resolve to exactly one datastore cluster. |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.StorageDrsConfigSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields, e.g. {"podConfigSpec": {"enabled": true, "defaultVmBehavior": "automated"}}. |

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |

#### `vmware_storage_recommend_datastores`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Compute (but do not apply) Storage DRS initial-placement/migration recommendations for a given placement spec. Read-only: it returns a list of recommendations for a caller to review and separately approve via vmware_storage_apply_drs_recommendation(_to_pod) — nothing is moved or reconfigured by this call itself (see this file's top doc comment for why this deviates from Tier 2). storage_spec must be a types.StoragePlacementSpec JSON object matching its Go struct field names exactly ("type": "create"|"clone"|"relocate"|"reconfigure", "podSelectionSpec": {"initialVmConfig": [{"storagePod": {"type":"StoragePod","value":"..."}, "disk": [...]}]}, etc.) — this is a real, fairly complex/polymorphic struct; a caller needs to know the underlying govmomi field names (same MVP limitation already accepted elsewhere in this project for complex specs, e.g. generated_vm_provisioning.go's CustomizationSpec). Fields requiring a genuinely polymorphic Go type (e.g. configSpec.deviceChange) cannot be supplied through this tool at all — vim25/types has no custom JSON unmarshaling for those, so submitting one fails to decode; omit configSpec.deviceChange and leave any per-disk placement.disk lists empty to still get a valid per-datastore recommendation list.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_storage_recommend_datastores(storage_spec)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `storage_spec` | object | sim | A types.StoragePlacementSpec JSON object — see this tool's description for field-name and polymorphic-field caveats. |

#### `vmware_storage_refresh_drs_recommendation`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Force Storage DRS to recompute its recommendations for a datastore cluster (StoragePod) right now, instead of waiting for its next scheduled interval. No configuration change, but classified alongside the other Storage DRS mutating actions here per the plan's Fase 1a severity table (see vmware_host_storage_refresh/vmware_vm_refresh_storage_info for the same convention).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_storage_refresh_drs_recommendation(confirm, pod)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `pod` | string | sim | Datastore cluster (StoragePod) name/pattern (e.g. "pod1") or a full inventory path. Must resolve to exactly one datastore cluster. |

#### `vmware_task_cancel`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Request cancellation of a running task. Best-effort: vSphere/vcsim accepts the cancel request and marks the task cancelled, but does not necessarily interrupt work already in flight (a task that is nearly done may still complete normally). Fails if the task has already completed.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_task_cancel(confirm, task)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `task` | string | sim | Managed object reference VALUE of the task (e.g. "task-123" — NOT "Task:task-123"; the type is always "Task"). This server has no tool today that hands you one directly (see this file's top doc comment) — obtain it from another source (e.g. vCenter's own API/UI) that surfaces a live task moref. |

#### `vmware_task_set_description`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Update a task's description (the localized message describing its current phase). Fails if the task has already completed.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_task_set_description(confirm, description, task)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `description` | object | sim | A types.LocalizableMessage JSON object matching its Go struct fields (e.g. {"key": "com.example.phase1", "message": "Phase 1"}). |
| `task` | string | sim | Managed object reference VALUE of the task (e.g. "task-123" — NOT "Task:task-123"; the type is always "Task"). This server has no tool today that hands you one directly (see this file's top doc comment) — obtain it from another source (e.g. vCenter's own API/UI) that surfaces a live task moref. |

#### `vmware_task_set_state`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Directly set a task's state (queued/running/success/error), optionally with a result value and/or a fault message. Fails if the task has already completed — see this file's top doc comment for "fault_message"'s narrowed representation vs. the real API's polymorphic fault type.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_task_set_state(confirm, state, task, [fault_message, result])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `fault_message` | string | — | Localized message for a generic fault. Only meaningful when state is "error". Optional. |
| `result` | object | — | Arbitrary JSON value to record as the task's result. Optional. |
| `state` | string | sim | New task state. |
| `task` | string | sim | Managed object reference VALUE of the task (e.g. "task-123" — NOT "Task:task-123"; the type is always "Task"). This server has no tool today that hands you one directly (see this file's top doc comment) — obtain it from another source (e.g. vCenter's own API/UI) that surfaces a live task moref. |

#### `vmware_task_update_progress`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Set a task's percentage-done value (0-100; out-of-range values are clamped server-side). Fails unless the task is currently running.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_task_update_progress(confirm, percent_done, task)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `percent_done` | integer | sim | 0-100. |
| `task` | string | sim | Managed object reference VALUE of the task (e.g. "task-123" — NOT "Task:task-123"; the type is always "Task"). This server has no tool today that hands you one directly (see this file's top doc comment) — obtain it from another source (e.g. vCenter's own API/UI) that surfaces a live task moref. |

#### `vmware_task_wait`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Block until a task finishes (successfully or with an error) and return its final info (state, result, error, progress). Fuses object.Task's Wait/WaitEx/WaitForResult/WaitForResultEx into one tool — see this file's top doc comment for why. Bounded by timeout_seconds (default 300).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_task_wait(task, [timeout_seconds])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `task` | string | sim | Managed object reference VALUE of the task (e.g. "task-123" — NOT "Task:task-123"; the type is always "Task"). This server has no tool today that hands you one directly (see this file's top doc comment) — obtain it from another source (e.g. vCenter's own API/UI) that surfaces a live task moref. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | — | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever. Default 300 (5 minutes) if omitted. |

### vApp (6)

#### `vmware_vapp_clone`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Clone a vApp (and every VM in it) into a new vApp under a target resource pool.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vapp_clone(confirm, name, spec, target_resource_pool, vapp)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `name` | string | sim | Name for the new (cloned) vApp. |
| `spec` | object | sim | A types.VAppCloneSpec JSON object matching its Go struct field names. "location" (a Datastore moref, e.g. {"type":"Datastore","value":"<datastore moref value>"}) is documented as required by the real API, though vcsim's simulator neither enforces nor uses it. "host", "resourceSpec", "vmFolder" are optional — see referencia/govmomi/vim25/types/types.go's VAppCloneSpec for the full field list. |
| `target_resource_pool` | string | sim | Resource pool identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "Resources") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/host/esxi-01.local/Resources") as returned by vmware_list_resource_pools. Must resolve to exactly one resource pool. |
| `vapp` | string | sim | vApp identifier: a name/pattern or a full inventory path under the datacenter's "vm" folder (vApps live in the VM inventory tree, resolved via Finder.VirtualApp — not the resource-pool "host" tree Finder.ResourcePool uses, even though a VirtualApp embeds a ResourcePool). Must resolve to exactly one vApp. |

#### `vmware_vapp_create_child_vm`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new virtual machine as a child of a vApp.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vapp_create_child_vm(config, confirm, vapp, [host])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `config` | object | sim | A types.VirtualMachineConfigSpec JSON object matching its Go struct field names — at minimum "name" and "files":{"vmPathName":"[datastore1] my-vm"} are needed for the VM to actually be created; the caller needs to know the full struct's field names for anything beyond that (same MVP limitation as this project's other raw-VirtualMachineConfigSpec tools). |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host` | string | — | Target ESXi host identifier (see vmware_list_hosts). Optional — omit to let vSphere pick. |
| `vapp` | string | sim | vApp identifier: a name/pattern or a full inventory path under the datacenter's "vm" folder (vApps live in the VM inventory tree, resolved via Finder.VirtualApp — not the resource-pool "host" tree Finder.ResourcePool uses, even though a VirtualApp embeds a ResourcePool). Must resolve to exactly one vApp. |

#### `vmware_vcenter_deploy_library_item`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Deploy a VM from an OVF library item. Returns the inventory path of the deployed VM. See this file's top doc comment for a vcsim content-upload gap that makes a full deploy fail server-side for OVF items created via vmware_vcenter_create_ovf (no uploaded OVF content) — this tool is expected to reach the server cleanly in that case, not necessarily succeed.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vcenter_deploy_library_item(confirm, library_item_id, [deployment_spec, target])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `deployment_spec` | object | — | OVF deployment spec. "default_datastore" (an inventory path, resolved automatically) is this project's friendlier alternative to the raw "default_datastore_id" field — give at most one. Every other field (network_mappings, storage_mappings, additional_parameters, storage_provisioning, storage_profile_id, locale, flags, vm_config_spec) is passed through verbatim to vcenter.DeploymentSpec — these reference OVF-package-internal keys or storage-policy IDs, not inventory paths. |
| `library_item_id` | string | sim | Content Library item ID (e.g. as returned by vmware_vcenter_create_template/vmware_vcenter_create_ovf, or listed by another content-library tool). |
| `target` | object | — | Deployment target. Each field, if given, is a full inventory path, not a raw vCenter object ID. |

| `placement` | object | — | Deployment target. Each field, if given, is a full inventory path, not a raw vCenter object ID. |

| `deployment_spec` | object | — | OVF deployment spec. "default_datastore" (an inventory path, resolved automatically) is this project's friendlier alternative to the raw "default_datastore_id" field — give at most one. Every other field (network_mappings, storage_mappings, additional_parameters, storage_provisioning, storage_profile_id, locale, flags, vm_config_spec) is passed through verbatim to vcenter.DeploymentSpec — these reference OVF-package-internal keys or storage-policy IDs, not inventory paths. |
| `library_item_id` | string | sim | Source OVF library item ID to deploy. |
| `target` | object | — | Deployment target. Each field, if given, is a full inventory path, not a raw vCenter object ID. |
| `template` | object | sim | Same shape as vmware_vcenter_create_template's top-level arguments (name, library_id, placement, disk_storage, disk_storage_overrides, vm_home_storage). source_vm is optional here — if omitted, the OVF is deployed first and the resulting VM used as the source, then destroyed after the template is created. |

### Virtual Disk (VDDK) (11)

#### `vmware_virtual_disk_copy`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Copy a virtual disk (vmdk), optionally converting its format (thin/thick/adapter type) per dest_spec. Classic VirtualDiskManager-scoped variant — requires an explicit source/destination datacenter, unlike the newer per-datastore file-manager copy tool.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_virtual_disk_copy(confirm, dest_datacenter, dest_datastore, dest_path, dest_spec, source_datacenter, source_datastore, source_path, [force])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `dest_datacenter` | string | sim | Destination datacenter name/pattern (e.g. "ha-datacenter") as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. Must resolve to exactly one datacenter — required by VirtualDiskManager's SOAP API even though dest_datastoredatastore already narrows the search (see this file's top doc comment, deviation 2). |
| `dest_datastore` | string | sim | Destination datastore name/pattern (e.g. "LocalDS_0") as returned by vmware_list_datastores. Must resolve to exactly one datastore. |
| `dest_path` | string | sim | Path to the Destination disk's .vmdk file relative to the datastore root, e.g. "disks/disk1.vmdk". Combined with dest_datastoredatastore to build the vSphere-internal "[datastore] path" datastore-path string VirtualDiskManager expects — no need to hand-format that bracket notation yourself. |
| `dest_spec` | object | sim | A types.FileBackedVirtualDiskSpec JSON object matching its Go struct field names, e.g. {"diskType":"thin","adapterType":"lsiLogic","capacityKb":1048576}. Governs how the destination disk is written (thin/thick, adapter type); the destination's actual size always comes from the source disk being copied, capacityKb here is only consulted for certain conversions. Accepted via generic JSON decode — see this file's top doc comment, deviation 3, for why FileBackedVirtualDiskSpec (not the bare VirtualDiskSpec) is required. |
| `force` | boolean | — | Overwrite the destination disk if it already exists. Default false. |
| `source_datacenter` | string | sim | Source datacenter name/pattern (e.g. "ha-datacenter") as returned by vmware_list_datacenters. Must resolve to exactly one datacenter — required by VirtualDiskManager's SOAP API even though source_datastoredatastore already narrows the search (see this file's top doc comment, deviation 2). |
| `source_datastore` | string | sim | Source datastore name/pattern (e.g. "LocalDS_0") as returned by vmware_list_datastores. Must resolve to exactly one datastore. |
| `source_path` | string | sim | Path to the Source disk's .vmdk file relative to the datastore root, e.g. "disks/disk1.vmdk". Combined with source_datastoredatastore to build the vSphere-internal "[datastore] path" datastore-path string VirtualDiskManager expects — no need to hand-format that bracket notation yourself. |

#### `vmware_vm_acquire_ticket`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `kind` | string | sim | Ticket type, e.g. "webmks" or "guestControl". |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_vm_add_device`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Add a new virtual device to a VM. MVP scope: device_type "disk" creates a brand new virtual disk file on a datastore; device_type "cdrom" adds a CD-ROM drive, optionally with an ISO already mounted. To attach an EXISTING disk file instead of creating one, use vmware_vm_attach_disk.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_add_device(confirm, device_type, vm, [capacity_kb, controller_type, datastore, file_name, iso_path, thin_provisioned])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `capacity_kb` | integer | — | New disk size in kilobytes. Required when device_type is "disk"; ignored for "cdrom". |
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `controller_type` | string | — | Disk controller type to attach the new disk to: "scsi" (default), "ide", "sata", or "nvme". A controller of that type must already exist on the VM. Only applies to device_type "disk". |
| `datastore` | string | — | Datastore name/pattern (e.g. "datastore1") as returned by vmware_list_datastores, to place the new disk file on. Required when device_type is "disk"; ignored for "cdrom". |
| `device_type` | string | sim | Which kind of device to add. Only "disk" and "cdrom" are supported in this MVP scope. |
| `file_name` | string | — | vmdk file name/path inside the datastore, e.g. "myvm/disk2.vmdk". Optional for device_type "disk" — if omitted, vSphere auto-names the file. Ignored for "cdrom". |
| `iso_path` | string | — | Datastore path of the ISO to mount, in bracketed form, e.g. "[datastore1] ISOs/ubuntu-24.04.iso" (combine a datastore name from vmware_list_datastores with a path uploaded via vmware_datastore_upload_file). Only applies to device_type "cdrom". If omitted, an empty CD-ROM drive (no media) is added. |
| `thin_provisioned` | boolean | — | Thin-provision the new disk. Default true. Only applies to device_type "disk". |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_vm_attach_disk`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Attach an EXISTING virtual disk file already present on a datastore to a VM. This does NOT create a new disk — use vmware_vm_add_device with device_type "disk" for that.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_attach_disk(confirm, datastore, id, vm, [controller_key, unit_number])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `controller_key` | integer | — | Key of the controller device to attach the disk to. Optional — omit to let vSphere pick. |
| `datastore` | string | sim | Datastore name/pattern where the disk identified by id lives. |
| `id` | string | sim | Identifier (datastore-relative vmdk path) of the existing virtual disk to attach. |
| `unit_number` | integer | — | Unit number on the controller to attach at. Optional — omit to let vSphere pick. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_vm_clone`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Clone a virtual machine into a new VM. Starts a long-running task; this call blocks until it completes (or fails).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_clone(confirm, folder, name, spec, vm)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `folder` | string | sim | Destination inventory folder for the clone: a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm") or a subfolder name/pattern under the datacenter's "vm" folder, resolved the same way vmArg/hostArg are (see dcScopedPath in finder.go). |
| `name` | string | sim | Name for the new (cloned) VM. |
| `spec` | object | sim | types.VirtualMachineCloneSpec as a JSON object matching its Go struct field names, e.g. {"location":{"pool":"<resource pool moref value>","datastore":"<datastore moref value>"},"powerOn":false,"template":false}. "location" is always required by vSphere; on a topology with only one implicit resource pool (e.g. standalone ESXi) an empty {} location is enough. See referencia/govmomi/vim25/types/types.go's VirtualMachineCloneSpec/VirtualMachineRelocateSpec for the full field list — accepted via generic JSON decode, not a hand-built recursive schema. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

Dry-run check of whether an existing virtual machine is compatible with a specific host and/or resource pool (e.g. before a manual migration), without moving it. Read-only — requires vCenter (object.VmCompatibilityChecker is not available on standalone ESXi).

| `pool` | string | — | Resource pool identifier: a name/pattern as returned (as an inventory path) by vmware_list_resource_pools. |
| `test_types` | array&lt;string&gt; | — | Optional list of types.CheckTestType values to limit which checks run. Omit to run every applicable check. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

At least one of vm, host, or pool is required (used to resolve the host(s) being checked against). Read-only — requires vCenter (object.VmCompatibilityChecker is not available on standalone ESXi).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_compatibility_check_config(spec, [host, pool, test_types, vm])`

| `host` | string | — | Host identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "esxi-01.local") or a full inventory path as returned by vmware_list_hosts. Must resolve to exactly one host. |
| `pool` | string | — | Resource pool identifier: a name/pattern as returned (as an inventory path) by vmware_list_resource_pools. |
| `spec` | object | sim | types.VirtualMachineConfigSpec as a JSON object matching its Go struct field names, e.g. {"numCPUs":4,"memoryMB":8192,"guestId":"otherGuest64"}. Accepted via generic JSON decode. |
| `test_types` | array&lt;string&gt; | — | Optional list of types.CheckTestType values to limit which checks run. Omit to run every applicable check. |
| `vm` | string | — | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_vm_create_secondary`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Turn on vSphere Fault Tolerance for a virtual machine by creating and powering on its secondary VM. The primary VM becomes fault tolerant once the secondary is created. Reversible via vmware_vm_turn_off_fault_tolerance.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_create_secondary(confirm, vm, [host])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host` | string | — | Host identifier (name/pattern or full inventory path, see vmware_list_hosts) where the secondary VM should be placed/powered on. Optional — omit to let vSphere pick a compatible host automatically. If the secondary VM is not compatible with an explicitly given host, the operation fails. |
| `vm` | string | sim | Primary virtual machine identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. For vmware_vm_disable_secondary/enable_secondary/make_primary/terminate_fault_tolerant/turn_off_fault_tolerance, this must be the PRIMARY VM of the fault tolerant group — these operations "can only be invoked from the primary virtual machine in the group" per the underlying API. |

#### `vmware_vm_create_secondary_ex`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Turn on vSphere Fault Tolerance for a virtual machine, like vmware_vm_create_secondary, but additionally accepting an explicit FaultToleranceConfigSpec (storage placement for the tie-breaker file, secondary config file, and secondary disks). Reversible via vmware_vm_turn_off_fault_tolerance.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_create_secondary_ex(confirm, vm, [host, spec])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `host` | string | — | Host identifier (name/pattern or full inventory path, see vmware_list_hosts) where the secondary VM should be placed/powered on. Optional — omit to let vSphere pick a compatible host automatically. If the secondary VM is not compatible with an explicitly given host, the operation fails. |
| `spec` | object | — | A types.FaultToleranceConfigSpec JSON object matching its Go struct fields (e.g. {"secondaryVmSpec": {...}, "metaDataPath": {...}}). Optional — omit for system defaults. |
| `vm` | string | sim | Primary virtual machine identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. For vmware_vm_disable_secondary/enable_secondary/make_primary/terminate_fault_tolerant/turn_off_fault_tolerance, this must be the PRIMARY VM of the fault tolerant group — these operations "can only be invoked from the primary virtual machine in the group" per the underlying API. |

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Apply a guest OS customization spec (network settings, hostname, sysprep/cloud-init identity, etc.) to a virtual machine. The VM must be powered off. Takes effect on next power-on.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_customize(confirm, spec, vm)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `spec` | object | sim | types.CustomizationSpec as a JSON object matching its Go struct field names, e.g. {"globalIPSettings":{},"nicSettingMap":[],"identity":{...}}. "identity" is polymorphic (types.BaseCustomizationIdentitySettings, e.g. a Sysprep/Linux/CloudinitPrep variant) — this tool accepts it via generic JSON decode into the field names of the concrete Go struct you intend, there is no schema-guided discriminator for which variant to use. See referencia/govmomi/vim25/types/types.go's CustomizationSpec for the full field list. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_vm_dataset_create_data_set`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new data set on a virtual machine (requires vSphere 8.0+ and VM hardware version 20+). Returns the new data set's identifier.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_dataset_create_data_set(confirm, spec, vm)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `spec` | object | sim | A dataset.CreateSpec JSON object (matching its Go struct's json tags). Required: "name" (form "com.company.project" recommended, to avoid collisions), "host" (One of "NONE", "READ_ONLY", "READ_WRITE". — controls ESXi/vCenter API access to entries), "guest" (One of "NONE", "READ_ONLY", "READ_WRITE". — controls in-guest VMware Guest SDK access to entries). Optional: "description", "omit_from_snapshot_and_clone" (bool, default false — if true, the data set is destroyed when the VM is reverted to a snapshot taken before it existed, and is not carried over by clones). |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identified by its raw vCenter REST API ID (e.g. "vm-21") — the SAME string as the VM's SOAP managed-object-reference Value (see vmware_vm_info's moref, or object.VirtualMachine.Reference().Value in govmomi). This domain does NOT resolve a name/inventory-path pattern the way most other tools' "vm" argument does — pass the raw ID directly (confirmed against govc's own vm.dataset.* CLI commands, which do exactly this). |

| `vm` | string | sim | VM identified by its raw vCenter REST API ID (e.g. "vm-21") — the SAME string as the VM's SOAP managed-object-reference Value (see vmware_vm_info's moref, or object.VirtualMachine.Reference().Value in govmomi). This domain does NOT resolve a name/inventory-path pattern the way most other tools' "vm" argument does — pass the raw ID directly (confirmed against govc's own vm.dataset.* CLI commands, which do exactly this). |

Must resolve to exactly one VM. #### `vmware_vm_export`

Start an OVF export lease for a virtual machine and return the downloadable device (VMDK/OVF) URLs once the lease is ready. NOTE: not simulated by this project's test harness (vcsim has no ExportVm handler) — exercise carefully against a real vCenter/ESXi first.

Must resolve to exactly one VM. For vmware_vm_disable_secondary/enable_secondary/make_primary/terminate_fault_tolerant/turn_off_fault_tolerance, this must be the PRIMARY VM of the fault tolerant group — these operations "can only be invoked from the primary virtual machine in the group" per the underlying API. |

NOTE: not simulated by this project's test harness (vcsim has no MigrateVMTask handler) — exercise carefully against a real vCenter first.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_migrate(confirm, vm, [host, priority, resource_pool, state])`

| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |

| `priority` | string | — | Task scheduling priority (types.VirtualMachineMovePriority). Default "defaultPriority" if omitted. |
| `resource_pool` | string | — | Destination resource pool identifier: a name/pattern as returned (as an inventory path) by vmware_list_resource_pools. Omit to leave the resource pool unchanged (host must then be given). |
| `state` | string | — | Desired power state after the migration (types.VirtualMachinePowerState). Omit to leave the power state unchanged. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_vm_promote_disks`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Promote a virtual machine's delta-disk-backed disks by consolidating their delta chain into the base disk. Omit/empty "disks" to promote every eligible disk (vSphere's documented default when the list is unset or empty) — the common case.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_promote_disks(confirm, vm, [disks, unlink])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |

| `disks` | array&lt;object&gt; | — | Advanced: specific disks to promote instead of every eligible disk. Each element is a types.VirtualDisk JSON object matching its Go struct field names (must include a "key" matching an existing virtual disk device on the VM). Omit for the common case (promote everything eligible). |
| `unlink` | boolean | — | Unlink the promoted disks from their delta chain as part of promotion. Default false. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_vm_query_changed_disk_areas`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Query which byte ranges of a virtual disk changed since a given point, using Changed Block Tracking (CBT). CBT must already be enabled and a changeId recorded for the disk (typically via a prior snapshot taken with CBT on) — otherwise this fails with "CBT is not enabled on disk". Passing offset equal to the disk's real capacity is a valid trivial call that returns a zero-length result without needing CBT at all (useful to confirm the tool/disk resolve correctly).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_query_changed_disk_areas(base_snapshot, disk_key, offset, vm, [cur_snapshot])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `base_snapshot` | string | sim | Managed object reference value (e.g. "snapshot-123") of the snapshot to diff from. Required — the underlying API dereferences this unconditionally. |
| `cur_snapshot` | string | — | Managed object reference value of the snapshot representing "now". Omit to use the VM's current state (only valid while the VM is powered off). |
| `disk_key` | integer | sim | Key of the virtual disk device on this VM (see vmware_vm_device). |
| `offset` | integer | sim | Byte offset to start computing changes from. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_vm_terminate_fault_tolerant`

**Modo:** `vcenter-only`  *(destrutiva)*

Terminate one secondary VM (or, if secondary_vm is omitted, ALL secondary VMs) in a fault tolerant group, invoked from the primary VM, allowing fault tolerance protection to lapse for that secondary. A terminated secondary may be respawned later (potentially on a different host) via vmware_vm_create_secondary/enable_secondary.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_terminate_fault_tolerant(confirm, vm, [secondary_vm])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `secondary_vm` | string | — | Secondary VM to terminate (name/pattern or full inventory path). Optional — omit to terminate ALL secondary VMs in the group. |
| `vm` | string | sim | Primary virtual machine identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. For vmware_vm_disable_secondary/enable_secondary/make_primary/terminate_fault_tolerant/turn_off_fault_tolerance, this must be the PRIMARY VM of the fault tolerant group — these operations "can only be invoked from the primary virtual machine in the group" per the underlying API. |

Must resolve to exactly one VM. For vmware_vm_disable_secondary/enable_secondary/make_primary/terminate_fault_tolerant/turn_off_fault_tolerance, this must be the PRIMARY VM of the fault tolerant group — these operations "can only be invoked from the primary virtual machine in the group" per the underlying API. |

#### `vmware_vm_unregister`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`  *(destrutiva)*

Remove a virtual machine from inventory WITHOUT deleting its files from the datastore (unlike vmware_vm_destroy, which is irreversible and deletes everything). The files remain and could theoretically be re-registered via their .vmx path, but this tool does not track or expose that path, so treat this as effectively irreversible from this server's point of view. Kept at Tier 1 (the AST classifier's fail-safe default) rather than downgraded, since re-registration isn't something this tool can do for the caller. The VM must already be powered off (vmware_vm_power_off) — vSphere rejects unregistering a powered-on VM, and this tool does not power it off for you (same precondition as vmware_vm_destroy).

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_unregister(confirm, vm)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_vm_wait_for_ip`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Block until a virtual machine's guest.ipAddress property reports an IP address. Requires VMware Tools running in the guest. Bounded by timeout_seconds (default 300) — returns an error instead of blocking forever if no IP is ever reported.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_wait_for_ip(vm, [timeout_seconds, v4])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | — | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever. Default 300 (5 minutes) if omitted. |
| `v4` | boolean | — | Wait specifically for an IPv4 address (an IPv6 address may be reported first otherwise). Default false (accept the first address reported, v4 or v6). |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_vm_wait_for_net_ip`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Block until every (or a specific) NIC on a virtual machine reports a guest IP address, keyed by MAC address. Requires VMware Tools running in the guest. Bounded by timeout_seconds (default 300) — returns an error instead of blocking forever if no IP is ever reported.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_wait_for_net_ip(vm, [device, timeout_seconds, v4])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `device` | array&lt;string&gt; | — | Wait only for these NICs, identified by MAC address or device name (e.g. "ethernet-0"). Omit to wait for every NIC. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | — | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever. Default 300 (5 minutes) if omitted. |
| `v4` | boolean | — | Only consider IPv4 addresses. Default true. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_vm_wait_for_power_state`

**Modo:** `vsphere-general`

Block until a virtual machine reaches the given power state. Returns immediately if it is already in that state. Bounded by timeout_seconds (default 300) — returns an error instead of blocking forever if the VM never reaches the requested state.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_vm_wait_for_power_state(state, vm, [timeout_seconds])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `state` | string | sim | Power state to wait for. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | — | Give up after this many seconds and return an error instead of blocking forever. Default 300 (5 minutes) if omitted. |
| `vm` | string | sim | VM identifier: a name/pattern (e.g. "cac-WN02") or a full inventory path (e.g. "/ha-datacenter/vm/cac-WN02") as returned by vmware_list_vms. Must resolve to exactly one VM. |

#### `vmware_cloudaws_sddc_create`

**Modo:** `cloud-aws`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new SDDC (POST /vmc/api/orgs/{org}/sddcs) — the single most expensive operation in this whole API: it provisions real physical ESXi hosts on AWS bare metal, billed hourly from the moment they come up. Known example body fields: num_hosts (int), name (string), provider ("AWS"), region (e.g. "US_WEST_2") — the real VMC API accepts many more optional fields (VPC/subnet, deployment_type, sddc_type, account_link config, etc.) not enumerated here; consult VMware's own VMC API docs for the full spec and pass them via "spec".

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_cloudaws_sddc_create(confirm, org, spec)`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `org` | string | sim | VMC on AWS organization ID (opaque identifier — visible in the VMC console URL, or via an orgs-listing tool). |
| `spec` | object | sim | SDDC creation spec — JSON object, e.g. {"num_hosts":1,"name":"my-sddc","provider":"AWS","region":"US_WEST_2"}. |

| `org` | string | sim | VMC on AWS organization ID (opaque identifier — visible in the VMC console URL, or via an orgs-listing tool). |
| `sddc` | string | sim | SDDC ID (opaque identifier returned by vmware_cloudaws_sddc_list/vmware_cloudaws_sddc_create). |
| `spec` | object | — | SddcPublicIp update document — JSON object, optional, fields per VMware's VMC API docs. |

## VMware Workstation Pro (28)

### Workstation Pro (28)

#### `vmware_workstation_nic_create`

**Modo:** `workstation`  *(destrutiva)*

Create a new network adapter in a VMware Workstation Pro VM (POST /vms/{id}/nic). Requires VMware Workstation Pro's vmrest service to be running locally on the machine where mcpvmware-mcp.exe executes — if the MCP server runs on a different machine than the one with Workstation Pro installed, this tool has no target to reach.

**Sintaxe:** `vmware_workstation_nic_create(confirm, id, type, [vmnet])`

| Parametro | Tipo | Obrig. | Descricao |
|---|---|:--:|---|
| `confirm` | boolean | sim | Must be exactly true to run. The server also requires --allow-destructive/VCENTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE to be enabled at startup — this argument alone is not enough. |
| `id` | string | sim | VM identifier, as returned by vmware_workstation_vm_list. |
| `type` | string | sim | Network adapter connection type. "custom" requires "vmnet" to select the specific virtual network (e.g. "vmnet8"); "bridged"/"hostonly"/"nat" ignore "vmnet" and use the host's default network of that kind. |
| `vmnet` | string | — | Virtual network name (e.g. "vmnet8"), as returned by vmware_workstation_vmnet_list — required only when type is "custom". |
